49	=== a14e9d762f Send error reports and crashes straight to Sentry, with readable stacks
50	The app's error reports used to go to JusPrin's server as five short text
51	fields, which passed them on to Sentry. They now go straight from the app
52	to Sentry through Sentry's own SDKs, and crashes are caught too. Kenneth:
53	"We want the Sentry server to capture as much info as possible so that we
54	can do production troubleshooting."
55	
56	What a report carries now
57	- The app uses sentry-native 0.17.5 (deps/Sentry) with the crashpad
58	  backend. Crashpad writes a crash's minidump from its own process,
59	  crashpad_handler, which ships beside the app on every platform. The SDK
60	  hands each envelope to OrcaSlicer's own HTTP client, which already knows
61	  the system's certificates and proxy.
62	- Nothing leaves without consent (the SDK's require_user_consent). With
63	  automatic reports on, reports and crashes go as they happen. With them
64	  off, only the one report the person chose to send goes; a crash stays on
65	  disk.
66	- Each event has what the SDK collects: the stack, the loaded modules, the
67	  machine, the recent steps (each page message's type and each tool call's
68	  outcome, never a payload), and this run's log file. It is filed by
69	  release, by what the app was doing and by the system, and grouped
70	  without the request ids that differ every time one failure happens.
71	- The stack is where the exception was thrown, not where the top handler
72	  reported it (Support/ThrowStack): the app's own __cxa_throw records
73	  each throw on macOS and Linux, and a vectored exception handler does it
74	  on Windows.
75	- The report's two older trims are deleted: the home folder is no longer
76	  replaced by "~", and fields are no longer cut to the old server's
77	  limits. Kenneth: "delete both older trims. no need to have these
78	  sentences be rewritten. they were close enough that we can tweak sentry
79	  server settings to meet them. No need to test the rules now."
80	
81	The Agent and Home pages
82	- Each page builds its event with @sentry/browser 11.10.0 and hands it to
83	  the app in its report_error message; the page itself never reaches the
84	  network for this. The app sends it like its own reports.
85	- On macOS and Linux the pages now load from jusprin:///<page>/index.html,
86	  served from resources/jusprin by a scheme handler each web view
87	  registers (Support/PageScheme). WKWebView and WebKitGTK tell a file://
88	  page only "Script error." about an uncaught error, with no file, line or
89	  stack, and Sentry's SDK drops that, so these errors never reached
90	  Sentry. The handler names each file's content type itself: on Linux,
91	  wxWidgets labels .html as application/xhtml+xml, and WebKitGTK would
92	  parse the page as XML. Windows keeps file://, where WebView2 reports the
93	  whole error.
94	- All web views share one handler, which lives as long as the app. On
95	  macOS wxWidgets gives WKWebView only a plain pointer to the handler, and
96	  WebKit can still ask it for a file after the view that registered it is
97	  gone; with a handler per view, the shell harness crashed there.
98	- Visible effect: on macOS and Linux, an uncaught page error that used to
99	  vanish now opens the "Something went wrong on our side" dialog, or is
100	  sent at once when automatic reports are on.
101	- Frames name the page the same way everywhere, app:///<page>/index.html,
102	  so one source map per page serves every platform. A Vite plugin writes
103	  that map for the script vite-plugin-singlefile inlines into index.html.
104	  New .gitattributes files keep the pages' sources in LF on every
105	  checkout, so every platform builds the same page.

107	Release and nightly builds

111	- macOS and Linux builds add line tables (-gline-tables-only) and split

=== 262fe08e91 Add the jusprin-release skill: every step of a JusPrin release
The release workflow refuses a commit without a version, release notes, a
guide check and the Sentry secrets, but nothing covered the steps it does
not enforce. The skill lists every step in order, and which of them need
Kenneth's yes.

- Every release is tested on all three platforms, twice (test suites, then
  the draft's files): macOS on this computer, Windows and Linux on the two
  test VMs, whose instructions stay in the local .claude/vm-harness folder,
  outside this public repository. An untested platform blocks the release.
- Set up: the main checkout has no changed tracked files and no unpushed
  commits; the range is fixed at a recorded commit; the version is settled
  before the release branch is made.
- Server: every address the app calls answers on the production server,
  checked against a made-up path that must answer 404, since maintenance
  mode answers 200 everywhere.
- Error-handling audit with the error-handling skill, then every test
  program on macOS, Windows and Linux (the release workflow builds and runs
  none), the live prompt suite when text the model reads changed, then the
  translation catalogs and the guide check.
- Any fix is its own commit, and the checks are redone for the grown range,
  also after the release commit has landed.
- Landing on jusprin-dev and moving main to the exact release commit, the
  release workflow, testing the draft's files including the Sentry checks
  (moved here from c27fdcbfeb), and what follows publishing.

Kenneth, 2026-11-17: "the local main checkout should be clear, no
uncommitted edits or unpushed commits, before anything can start".

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M7P293VQ5NG0821KH89WE15T
And: "The test on Mac should run on the current computer, and we have two
GCP VMs to run Windows and Linux".

=== e86a86f314 Shell harness: build on Linux and Windows again
3c134d39e3 added a call to snapshot_native_window in the printer window
check (--printer-window) without the #ifdef __APPLE__ that the function's
declaration has, so the shell harness stopped compiling on Linux and
Windows: "'snapshot_native_window' was not declared in this scope". The
call now has the same guard as the declaration and the harness's other
calls to it. On macOS the check still saves its pictures; elsewhere it
saves none.

Tested: on a Linux VM (gcc 13) the harness fails to compile with the guard
removed and compiles with it. On macOS the harness builds and
--printer-window still writes its pictures.

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M7NZ6K2AQY4ECQCB8HAA8MJ7

=== a14e9d762f Send error reports and crashes straight to Sentry, with readable stacks
The app's error reports used to go to JusPrin's server as five short text
fields, which passed them on to Sentry. They now go straight from the app
to Sentry through Sentry's own SDKs, and crashes are caught too. Kenneth:
"We want the Sentry server to capture as much info as possible so that we
can do production troubleshooting."

What a report carries now
- The app uses sentry-native 0.17.5 (deps/Sentry) with the crashpad
  backend. Crashpad writes a crash's minidump from its own process,
  crashpad_handler, which ships beside the app on every platform. The SDK
  hands each envelope to OrcaSlicer's own HTTP client, which already knows
  the system's certificates and proxy.
- Nothing leaves without consent (the SDK's require_user_consent). With
  automatic reports on, reports and crashes go as they happen. With them
  off, only the one report the person chose to send goes; a crash stays on
  disk.
- Each event has what the SDK collects: the stack, the loaded modules, the
  machine, the recent steps (each page message's type and each tool call's
  outcome, never a payload), and this run's log file. It is filed by
  release, by what the app was doing and by the system, and grouped
  without the request ids that differ every time one failure happens.
- The stack is where the exception was thrown, not where the top handler
  reported it (Support/ThrowStack): the app's own __cxa_throw records
  each throw on macOS and Linux, and a vectored exception handler does it
  on Windows.
- The report's two older trims are deleted: the home folder is no longer
  replaced by "~", and fields are no longer cut to the old server's
  limits. Kenneth: "delete both older trims. no need to have these
  sentences be rewritten. they were close enough that we can tweak sentry

An error is expected only when the person can do something about it and

entry point, and the person reads "Something went wrong on our side".

about, just show the user a generic error message and give user a way to
report a problem. On the back end though, we need to make sure we send as
much info as possible to the Sentry server so that we can do root cause
analysis. And that's it, nothing else."

Top handlers
- reported(doing, body), in Support/ErrorReport.hpp, wraps every CallAfter
  body, timer, HTTP callback and thread JusPrin's own code starts. Before,
  an exception from a CallAfter or a timer ended the main loop, and one from
  an HTTP callback or a thread called std::terminate: a model list entry
  without "id" aborted the app at launch (exit 134).
- report_unexpected_error moves itself to the main thread when called from
  another. A failure the person already answered in this run is not asked
  about again, so its dialog cannot reopen itself; automatic reports, which
  open no dialog, still send each one.
- An exception leaving any other native event stays OrcaSlicer's, as
  Kenneth decided; GUI_App::OnExceptionInMainLoop is unchanged.

- A failed request names its cause only where the person can act. On a
  JusPrin account, by the gateway's error code: signed out, out of credits,
  app too old, request too large, too many requests. With their own key, by
  the HTTP status alone: 401, 413, 429. No answer at all says the service
  could not be reached.

  cut short or unreadable throw UnexpectedServiceAnswer with the service's
  status, request id and body. The sentences for an overloaded, unavailable,
  timed-out, paused or cut-short service are deleted, and
  StreamEvent::Kind::Incomplete with them. The model declining to answer
  (stop reason "refusal") keeps its sentence: it is the model's answer, not
  a failure.

  and is also reported when automatic reports are on, with no dialog. A file
  the person picked that OrcaSlicer will not read answers "refused" and is
  not reported. When the saved projects cannot be read, the call's message

=== d010a88c1a Read printer sizes the same in every language
When JusPrin runs in a language that writes decimals with a comma
(Portuguese, German, French, Spanish, Russian and others), the add-printer
form showed no nozzle sizes for almost every printer, so the printer could
not be added. GitHub issue TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin#39 reports it for
the Flashforge Creator 5 Pro and its 0.4 mm nozzle.

wxWidgets sets the C library's number format to the app's language at
startup. JusPrin's printer catalog read the sizes in the printer profiles
with std::stod, which follows that format, so "0.4" read as 0. With the
number format set to Portuguese, 412 of 454 printer models lost their
nozzle sizes, and fractional bed sizes were cut short (233.5 mm read as
233). The same mistake read a 0.4 mm nozzle in an opened 3MF as 0, and
told the AI about a nozzle mismatch as "0,2" instead of "0.2".

On macOS the bug is usually hidden: an app opened from Finder has no LANG
setting, and the bundled Python's startup then resets the whole C locale
to "C". Python does this only on Unix, so Windows always shows the bug.

The catalog, the printer backend and the 3MF facts now parse with
OrcaSlicer's locale-independent string_to_double_decimal_point and
atof_decimal_point. The mismatch text is written by the JSON library
instead of snprintf. The test programs compile LocalesUtils.cpp directly,
as they do the JusPrin sources they test.

Tested: three new tests switch the number format to Portuguese; each fails
without this change and passes with it. jusprin_tests (180 cases) and
agent_bridge_tests (581 cases) pass, and the clang-tidy include check
passes on the changed lines. In the real app on macOS, started with LANG
set and the language set to Portuguese, JusPrin 2.0.0 showed no nozzle
size for the Creator 5 Pro and kept Continue disabled; this build showed
0.25, 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8 mm and added the printer with its 0.4 mm profile.
Not run on Windows.

Replaces the "Error handling discipline" list in AGENTS.md.

An error is expected only when the person can do something about it and
Kenneth decided what the product tells them. Every other error is
unexpected: no code where it happens, it travels up unchanged, and the one
handler at the top of the entry point reports it with everything known and
tells the person "Something went wrong on our side".

Kenneth, 2026-11-16: "if the error is something that user can do nothing
about, just show the user a generic error message and give user a way to
report a problem. On the back end though, we need to make sure we send as
much info as possible to the Sentry server so that we can do root cause
analysis. And that's it, nothing else."

The rules name the error-handling skill, which is not in this commit.

=== b3eed3bf4b Report unexpected errors to the JusPrin team, and fix four bugs found on the way
When something fails that no person can act on, JusPrin now shows one
dialog, "Something went wrong on our side" (boards agent-ui-11 to 16),
instead of a sentence about that particular failure. The person can see
the whole report, press "Report to JusPrin team", or tick "From now on,
report errors like this automatically". The report goes to JusPrin's
server (/ent/jusprin/v2/error_reports), which passes it to Sentry.

Why: under the error-handling rules, a failure with no outcome a person
decided travels up unchanged to the top of its entry point and is
reported there, instead of each site writing its own sentence. Kenneth
agreed to this on 2026-11-15: "Yes, go with this approach."

The reporting path
- Support/ErrorReport: report_unexpected_error() logs the error, then
  sends it at once when automatic reports are on, or queues it for the
  dialog after the current event. A failure that repeats while its dialog
  waits is queued once; after the person answers, the next occurrence
  opens the dialog again, and every occurrence is sent when reports are
  automatic (Kenneth: "leave it"). A report holds the app and OS versions,
  what the app was doing, the error and, for page errors, the stack. The
  home folder becomes "~", a file-system error's paths become "<path>",
  and each field is cut to the server's limit. The send is anonymous: no
  token or cookie.
- Shell/ErrorReportDialog: the dialog, drawn with the design tokens. Its
  line "no chat messages, no files, no project names and no account or
  email address" stays although other error text can quote a file name
  (Kenneth: "Keep the promise and accept the risk.").
- Top handlers: the AI pages' and Home's message handlers, the file
  picker's callback (it reads the chosen files after the page's message
  was handled), and both pages' own top level (window "error" and
  "unhandledrejection", sent as a new report_error message and queued
  until the page has connected).
- An exception that leaves any other native event is handled exactly as
  OrcaSlicer handles it; no OrcaSlicer-owned file is changed. Kenneth: "it
  should behave the same as the upstream. no reason to use a diff
  behavior here for the fork".
- Preferences › Updates: a new "Error reports" box, "Report errors to the
  JusPrin team automatically", off by default.

Five failures now take that path, with their sentences removed:
- "JusPrin couldn't start signing in. Try again." (the AI page and Home)
- "The file could not be read." (an attachment that is not base64, or a
  chosen or dropped file that cannot be opened or read)
- "The G-code couldn't be written to %s." (exporting from print history)
- "The panel is still loading. Try again in a moment." (a printer or
  filament chat asked to reply before its page sent its instructions; the
  person's message is then left with no reply under it, Kenneth: "leave
  it")
- "The earlier values cannot be put back." (an undo the settings preview
  refuses without giving a reason)

Six others stay as they are, on Kenneth's answer "Yes, keep them": signing
in that did not finish, an unreadable import from another app, the AI
models not loaded yet, the saved projects that could not be read, the open
project that could not be saved, and projects that could not be loaded.

New on-screen strings beyond the boards (the report's row names "App",
"Was doing" and "Where", the singular forms of the two counted sentences,
and the Preferences group, box and detail line) were shown to Kenneth, who
answered "approved". All new strings are machine-translated into the 22
catalogs and marked "# AI Translated"; two are also marked "Needs human
review" (the Lithuanian and Basque singular forms). The report line
"attaching the chosen files" was added after that and he has not seen it.

Four bugs, each reproduced in the running app before it was fixed
- A sign-in or API key that could not be saved says so. With the settings
  file unwritable the app showed "Signed in as …" or "Key saved on this
  computer" and lost both on quitting: the save step answered "saved"
  without looking at the write. It now answers from the settings, so
  Preferences shows the warnings it already had. The welcome screen and
  Home still show none; they have no place that draws it.
- An attachment the chat refused no longer stops the project saving. A
  .bin, a file over the size limit or one the project's folder would not
  take left a record naming a file that was never kept, and saving checks
  every named file, so every save failed until the person pressed Remove.
  A refused attachment now names no file.
- Deleting the account waits for a reply running in the main window. The
  Preferences window's host has no chat, so its check never saw the
  reply; it now asks the docked panel's host. The refusal still shows
  "Check your internet connection, then try again.", whose wording is to
  be decided. A reply in a printer or filament chat is not looked at.
- A chat whose account or key is gone still shows the model it ran on in
  its greyed picker, where it showed the default of whatever provider was
  left. The app sends the chat's own model with the provider's name.

Tests
- agent_bridge_tests (581 cases), jusprin_tests (178), the AgentUI tests
  (831) and the HomeUI tests (162) pass on this tree; tsc is clean. The
  attachment and model-picker tests failed on the old code.
- Shown in a scratch copy of the app (its own data folder and HOME, the
  local server, a stand-in Sentry; nothing went to the real one):
  - the four bugs, old build beside fixed build, and again on the build
    that holds everything here except the last change below;
  - the dialog for a sign-in that cannot start, an attachment that is not
    base64, a G-code export into a read-only folder, a printer chat whose
    page held back its instructions, and an error thrown in the AI page's
    own script; a report arriving; the Preferences box, and a report sent
    with no dialog once it is ticked;
  - two minutes of ordinary use with no dialog opening by itself.
- Not shown in the running app: the removal of the main-loop hook and the
  file picker's handler, which were made after those runs; an unreadable
  file chosen in the system's file dialog; and the undo refused without a
  reason, which cannot happen in the real app (the settings preview
  records a reason with every refusal).

=== 00953649de Translate JusPrin into upstream OrcaSlicer's 22 languages
JusPrin's own windows and its AI and Home pages showed English in every
language. Every string a person reads in them is now marked and translated
into the 22 languages upstream ships, in catalogs of the fork's own so that
taking an upstream release never conflicts in one:

- Localization/native/<lang>.po for native text, collected by
  Localization/update_catalogs.py (text upstream's template already has
  keeps upstream's translation) and merged by Brand/brand_catalogs.py into
  the catalog the app loads.
- Localization/pages/<lang>.po for both pages, through Lingui 5.9.5. The app
  passes its language as ?lang=; the page activates it before any module
  runs.

Text the model reads (prompts, skills, tool results), logs, error reports,
identifiers and names stay English. The translations are machine-made and
marked "# AI Translated"; entries a translator was unsure of also carry
"# Needs human review: <what to check>". Terms follow upstream's catalog
and the OrcaSlicer localization glossary.

Sentences that were built from translated pieces are now one message each,
with placeholders and plural forms, and render the same English. Other
changes the translation needed:

- Support/Translate.hpp: GUI-free code marks text with L() and translates it
  with translated() and translated_plural(), which the app installs.
- "Model" and "Search models" in the printer picker, and "Plate" in the
  add-printer form, have contexts of their own, apart from the AI model and
  the project plate.

  (Support/DecimalText on the native side, decimalText on the pages): a
  German app reads "Kobra 3 · 0,4 mm".
- An untitled chat is titled with the translated "New chat"; the saved
  document keeps its English default.
- "Ask current chat about this" drafts its message in the app's language.
- The setup card's estimate row wraps its link to the next line when a
  translation is too long to share the row.
- All settings shows OrcaSlicer's setting labels, groups and values through
  OrcaSlicer's own catalog.
- Translator notes sit on the line of the string they describe, so xgettext
  gives each note to the right string.

  forms; Home type-checks Lingui from its own packages.

box, page-link and email sign-in requests carry Accept-Language with the

have M." is built by the app from the gateway's cost and balance, and the

=== 5e173c5e15 Fix the shell harness runs that 6b59a887ca and the 2.5.0 merge broke
Commit 6b59a887ca fails a chat's turn when the chat's provider has no
stored key. The recorder, reply-choices and calibration runs use a mock
model with no key, so they hung on their second message, as the default
run did before 084b8d35a7. Those runs now store the placeholder key too.

Running every chat mode then showed other failures, not caused by that
commit, now fixed:

- A calibration made from a person's project lost its project and chat.
  OrcaSlicer's generator moves the project folder twice, and the flag
  that keeps the project going was used up by the first move. It now
  holds for the whole generation (ProjectPersistence).
- A calibration test reopened from Home did not say "Opened from Home".
  Opening replaces the document more than once, and the first
  replacement used up the mark. The mark now names the project id and is
  used only by that project's document.
- Autosave saved a project again after an idle wait. OrcaSlicer's
  project info panel creates an empty info record when it refreshes,
  and autosave counted that as a change. It now compares the record's
  contents, so no record and an empty one are the same.
- The calibration and setup-differences mocks sent one value for
  settings that hold one per nozzle type since the 2.5.0 merge
  (nozzle_temperature, initial_layer_speed); they send two now.
- Three checks expected stale text: Home says "Draft" for a project
  never printed, and the All settings panel heads a printer setting with
  its page and group ("Extruder · Retraction").
- The recorder now keeps a "busy" answer to a slice read made while the
  turn's own slice runs, which is what the app tells the model there.
  The README says how long recording takes and how those three points
  depend on timing.

The harness prints a failed tool's error code and message, not only its
empty result.

Tested on macOS: every chat mode of shell_integration_harness passes
(default, chat-restoration, file-opening, task-chat, account-box,
printer-chat-sheet, check-print, mcp, reply-choices, setup-differences,
timeline, calibration, tool-strip and reopen-prompt captures),
--autosave-seed and --autosave-reopen pass, and agent_bridge_tests
passes (577 cases). The workspace harness fails 2 checks
(second_model_dropped, model_added_to_a_project_is_an_edit), down from
11; those 2 failed before this change too. The recorder
(--project-prompt-requests) still fails 3 checks at the three points
where the turn's slice is running, because that slice can end partway
through the reads; requests.json is not recorded again here.

=== 084b8d35a7 Shell harness: the default run's mock AI has a key, as a person's would
Since 6b59a887ca the app keeps a chat the person has talked in on its
provider, and fails the next turn with "This chat ran on OpenAI, and no
OpenAI API key is set up now" when no key for it is stored. The harness's
default run installed its mock AI with the AI turned off and no key, a
state the app itself never reaches, so the chat's second message ("please
duplicate the selected object") failed that way and the run waited
forever for the tool to succeed.

The default run now stores a placeholder OpenAI key with the AI turned on,
as the configured task-chat capture already does, and points OpenAI at a
closed local port so the key never leaves the machine.

Tested: the default run passes, 631 checks with no failures; before, it
hung after 281. A temporary print showed the failing turn's error was
chat_provider_removed.

content.content:
JusPrin 2 is a major upgrade. We rebuilt nearly everything: it is now built on OrcaSlicer 2.5.0, and every project has AI working beside it. The goal is the one JusPrin started with: make 3D printing simpler for hobbyists. You tell AI what you are printing and what went wrong. AI reads your file, your settings and your slice, changes the settings and slices again.

## What AI can do

Each project has an AI chat beside the 3D view. Ask in plain words, and AI works in the open project:

- Set up the printer, filament and print settings for the part you are printing.
- Open a model or project file, place objects on the plate, and lay out plates.
- Cut, split, merge and repair objects.
- Change print settings for you.
- Slice the plate and check the result, for example support printed inside a hole, or a part that starts in the air.
- Look at a photo of a failed print and suggest what to change.
- Run a filament calibration test (temperature, flow or pressure advance), read a photo of the printed test, and save the result as a new filament preset.

When you ask AI to print, it opens the usual send dialog. You choose the options and press Send. AI never starts a print.

When a slice has a problem, a marker on the 3D view shows it. Press Ask AI to have AI explain the problem and your options.

## Ways to use AI

- Sign up for a JusPrin account in the app. New accounts get free credits, and no card is needed.
- Use your own OpenAI, Anthropic or OpenRouter API key.
- Connect an AI app you already use: Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop, Cowork, Cursor or VS Code. It can then work with the project open in JusPrin.
- Or skip AI and just slice.

## Also new

- **Home screen.** Your projects and printers are on one screen. Each printer card shows the printer's status, and once the printer is connected, opens its own window.
- **Printers.** Add a printer and connect it by chatting with AI. You can connect Bambu Lab printers in LAN mode, and Klipper (Moonraker) and OctoPrint printers.
- **Saving.** Projects save themselves, so JusPrin never asks you to save or discard. File › Save (Cmd+S on a Mac, Ctrl+S on Windows and Linux) keeps a version you can go back to in File › Version history. Saving doesn't write over the .3mf file you opened. To get a .3mf file, use File › Export › Project 3MF (Cmd+Shift+S or Ctrl+Shift+S).
- **Opening files.** A file you open from Finder or File Explorer opens as a new project. A model dropped on the 3D view is added to the open project.
- **Check print.** Print › Check print shows a report of the slice beside the preview.
- **Print history.** Every sliced file you export or send to a printer is listed on Home's Print history, and you can print it again from there.
- **Classic view.** View › Switch to classic view shows OrcaSlicer's full interface. Press Back to JusPrin to return.
- **Updates.** JusPrin checks its GitHub releases for a new version once a day. You see the result in Preferences › Updates.
- **Reporting a problem.** Help › Report a problem opens a new GitHub issue in your browser, with the app's version and your system filled in.

## Upgrading from JusPrin 1.4

- **Installing.** On Windows, the installer replaces JusPrin 1. On a Mac, JusPrin 2 is also called JusPrin.app, so dragging it to Applications replaces JusPrin 1. On Linux, the AppImage is a new file, and JusPrin 1's AppImage stays where it is.
- **Your printers.** The first time JusPrin 2 starts, it offers to import your printers from JusPrin 1 or OrcaSlicer, with their filaments and print settings. You choose which printers to import. You can import later with Printer › Import printers from JusPrin 1 or Import printers from OrcaSlicer.
- **Your JusPrin 1 folder.** JusPrin 2 keeps its settings in a new folder. It only reads JusPrin 1's folder and never changes it. JusPrin 1's app settings, such as units and language, aren't imported.
- **Your account.** Your JusPrin 1 sign-in doesn't carry over. To use AI with a JusPrin account, sign up in JusPrin 2, even if you had an account in JusPrin 1. Chats from JusPrin 1 aren't imported.

## Downloads

- **Windows (64-bit):** the installer, or the portable .zip, which runs without installing.
- **Mac:** one disk image for Macs with Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
- **Linux (64-bit):** an AppImage, built on Ubuntu 24.04. Make the file executable, then run it.
- **SHA256SUMS.txt** lists each file's checksum.

Questions or problems: write to jusprin-support@obico.io, or use Help › Report a problem in the app.
----
#pragma once

#include "libslic3r_version.h"

#include <string>

namespace Slic3r::GUI::JusPrin::Updates {

// JusPrin's own version: what Preferences shows and what the update check
// compares with the version in each JusPrin release tag. It is separate
// from SoftFever_VERSION, OrcaSlicer's version, which this build keeps
// because 3MF projects, profile updates, the user_backup-v<version> folder
// and AppConfig's upgrade logic all read it.
inline constexpr char kVersion[] = "2.0.0";

// The version a problem report or a saved chat names: JusPrin's and the
// OrcaSlicer release it is built on, as "JusPrin 2.0.0 (OrcaSlicer 2.5.0)".
// Not SLIC3R_VERSION, which is OrcaSlicer's Bambu network-plugin
// compatibility number (02.08.01.55), not a release anyone can look up.
inline std::string version_label() { return std::string("JusPrin ") + kVersion + " (OrcaSlicer " + SoftFever_VERSION + ")"; }

// The User-Agent of every request JusPrin sends to its own server, so the
// server can tell JusPrin releases apart. Orca's Http sends
// "JusPrin/<SoftFever_VERSION>" by default, which names the OrcaSlicer
// release and is the same for every JusPrin release built on it.
inline std::string user_agent() { return std::string("JusPrin/") + kVersion + " OrcaSlicer/" + SoftFever_VERSION; }

} // namespace Slic3r::GUI::JusPrin::Updates

namespace Slic3r::GUI::JusPrin::Updates {

// JusPrin's own version: what Preferences shows and what the update check
// compares with the version in each JusPrin release tag. It is separate
// from SoftFever_VERSION, OrcaSlicer's version, which this build keeps
// because 3MF projects, profile updates, the user_backup-v<version> folder
// and AppConfig's upgrade logic all read it.
inline constexpr char kVersion[] = "2.0.0";

// The version a problem report or a saved chat names: JusPrin's and the
// OrcaSlicer release it is built on, as "JusPrin 2.0.0 (OrcaSlicer 2.5.0)".
// Not SLIC3R_VERSION, which is OrcaSlicer's Bambu network-plugin
// compatibility number (02.08.01.55), not a release anyone can look up.
inline std::string version_label() { return std::string("JusPrin ") + kVersion + " (OrcaSlicer " + SoftFever_VERSION + ")"; }

// The User-Agent of every request JusPrin sends to its own server, so the
// server can tell JusPrin releases apart. Orca's Http sends
// "JusPrin/<SoftFever_VERSION>" by default, which names the OrcaSlicer
// release and is the same for every JusPrin release built on it.
inline std::string user_agent() { return std::string("JusPrin/") + kVersion + " OrcaSlicer/" + SoftFever_VERSION; }

} // namespace Slic3r::GUI::JusPrin::Updates

# JusPrin: Sentry's native SDK, which files JusPrin's error reports and
# catches crashes (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Support/SentryClient.cpp).
#
# The release zip, not the tag's archive: it carries crashpad and the other
# submodules. Crashpad writes a crash's minidump from its own process,
# crashpad_handler, which ships beside the app.
#
# The SDK sends nothing itself (SENTRY_TRANSPORT none): the app hands its
# events to OrcaSlicer's own HTTP client, which already knows the system's
# certificates and proxy on every platform. Crashpad uploads a crash from its
# handler with the system's own HTTP on macOS and Windows, and with curl on
# Linux, hence the curl dependency there.
set(_sentry_depends ${ZLIB_PKG})
if (CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME STREQUAL "Linux")
    list(APPEND _sentry_depends ${CURL_PKG})
endif ()

orcaslicer_add_cmake_project(Sentry
    URL https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-native/releases/download/0.17.5/sentry-native.zip
    URL_HASH SHA256=64d1e29f43116d236076fd751f11305e3b9e31ab14ecbb8d7058246b56f43991
    DEPENDS ${_sentry_depends}
    CMAKE_ARGS
        -DSENTRY_BACKEND:STRING=crashpad
        -DSENTRY_TRANSPORT:STRING=none
        -DSENTRY_BUILD_SHARED_LIBS:BOOL=OFF
        -DSENTRY_BUILD_TESTS:BOOL=OFF
        -DSENTRY_BUILD_EXAMPLES:BOOL=OFF
        -DSENTRY_BUILD_BENCHMARKS:BOOL=OFF
        -DSENTRY_INTEGRATION_QT:BOOL=OFF
)

content.content:
=== 25c280af8d JusPrin 2: server text in the app's language
The pages the JusPrin 2 app opens (prices, billing, cancel, purchase done),
the account box, the sentences /ent/jusprin/v2/account sends for the app to
show, and the sign-in code email are now translated into the app's 22
languages besides English, the same set OrcaSlicer ships.

How the language is chosen (jusprin/v2/language.py, a middleware for
/ent/jusprin/v2/ only, after Django's LocaleMiddleware): a ?lang= on a link,
then a jusprin_language cookie, then Accept-Language, then English. The app
sends its own language in Accept-Language. Its sheet is a web view that sends
the computer's language instead, so web_link stores the app's language with
the link (or puts ?lang= on a guest link) and the opened page sets the cookie,
which keeps the language through sign-out and Chargebee and back.

Sentences are whole translatable units: no English fragments are joined, and
counts use plural forms. Sentences placed one after another go through a
translatable joiner, so Japanese and Chinese have no space after their full
stop. Dates use a format each language supplies: the full month name in the
form the language writes after a day, or numbers where the month name would
need an elided article (Italian, Catalan) or end in a dot that doubles the
full stop (Lithuanian). Prices use a translatable "$%(amount)s".

The catalogs are machine-translated and marked "# AI Translated". The
compiled .mo files are committed (a .gitignore exception), as Obico's are,
because the web image doesn't compile catalogs; test_language.py fails when
an entry is untranslated or a .mo is behind its .po. The README's "JusPrin
2's server text" section says how to update them.

Chargebee's checkout and receipts, Obico's own sign-in pages, and the plan
names Hobby and Workshop stay English.

 web_ent/jusprin/v2/web.py                          |  261 +++--
 web_ent/settings_ent.py                            |    6 +-
 65 files changed, 22588 insertions(+), 180 deletions(-)
=== bcd0fc94b0 JusPrin 2: report every failure a person cannot act on, and take the app's error reports
A failure the person can do nothing about is answered "Something went wrong
on our side" and goes to Sentry with everything known about it. A failure
they can act on keeps its own answer. Kenneth, 2026-11-16: "if the error is
something that user can do nothing about, just show the user a generic error
message and give user a way to report a problem. On the back end though, we
need to make sure we send as much info as possible to the Sentry server so
that we can do root cause analysis. And that's it, nothing else."

The AI gateway (/ent/jusprin/v2/messages and /responses):
- The provider refusing a request (any status but 200 and 413), failing or
  going quiet partway through a reply, being unreachable or too slow, and the
  server's own slots for large requests being full all reach the one handler
  at the top of the endpoint. Before, a 400 was passed off as a 502, a
  failure inside a reply was recorded as a completed reply, and an outage or
  a timeout got an answer of its own and reached no Sentry.
- A completed reply that cannot be kept afterwards, and a chat title the app
  did not encode as UTF-8, reach the same handler. Before, the first was
  caught where it happened and the second was read with its bad bytes
  replaced.
- The report carries the provider's status, request id and error text, and
  the request's user, chat, turn, kind, alias, model and outcome.
- None of these is recorded as a completed reply or kept as one.
- Answers of their own, in errors.EXPECTED: signed out, out of credits, app
  too old, too many turns a minute, chat too large for the provider, and the
  four refusals of a print report.

The Django views: a failure reaches Sentry through its Django integration.
The app is told the same sentence as JSON; a page in the app's sheet shows it
in the app's language.

Checkout and cancel: Chargebee refusing a checkout or a cancel is not the
person's to act on, so it goes up; "Checkout couldn't start" and "The plan
couldn't be cancelled" are gone. So does a checkout that comes back in any
state but succeeded or cancelled, one that bought neither a JusPrin 2 plan
nor a pack, and one that is another account's. A checkout the person
cancelled goes back to the prices, as before.

POST /ent/jusprin/v2/error_reports takes an error report from the desktop app
and passes it to the Sentry project named by JUSPRIN_V2_APP_SENTRY_DSN. That
 web_ent/settings_ent.py                            |   3 +
 web_ent/urls_ent.py                                |   4 +
 68 files changed, 1340 insertions(+), 206 deletions(-)
=== e56ff4f1f1 JusPrin 2: keep one row for each start of the desktop app
The app posts to /ent/jusprin/v2/launches each time it starts, with the
random install id it made on its first start, its version label and what
the system calls itself. AppLaunch keeps one row per report: distinct ids
per day are installs in use, and an id's first row says when a download
became a running app. Nothing on a row names a person. Every release may
send one, so the view is not behind supported_app.

 web_ent/jusprin/v2/tests/test_launches.py     | 42 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 web_ent/jusprin/v2/urls.py                    |  4 ++-
 5 files changed, 135 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)
=== c9e2b0af85 JusPrin 2: PostHog page views and "app opened"
JusPrin 2's pages (Credits and plans, billing, checkout, cancel, the portal)
now load PostHog, in Obico's project, the one obico.io and app.obico.io send
to, so a visit to obico.io and a later JusPrin 2 page can be the same person.
The snippet is the one layout_ent.html loads. A signed-in person is named by
user id alone: no name or email goes to PostHog.

No page sees the desktop app open, so the server sends one event itself:
"app opened", the first time each day (UTC) a signed-in app reads its account.
It carries the same user id and the app's release, and nothing about the

=== 25c280af8d JusPrin 2: server text in the app's language
The pages the JusPrin 2 app opens (prices, billing, cancel, purchase done),
the account box, the sentences /ent/jusprin/v2/account sends for the app to
show, and the sign-in code email are now translated into the app's 22
languages besides English, the same set OrcaSlicer ships.

How the language is chosen (jusprin/v2/language.py, a middleware for
/ent/jusprin/v2/ only, after Django's LocaleMiddleware): a ?lang= on a link,
then a jusprin_language cookie, then Accept-Language, then English. The app
sends its own language in Accept-Language. Its sheet is a web view that sends
the computer's language instead, so web_link stores the app's language with
the link (or puts ?lang= on a guest link) and the opened page sets the cookie,
which keeps the language through sign-out and Chargebee and back.

Sentences are whole translatable units: no English fragments are joined, and
counts use plural forms. Sentences placed one after another go through a
translatable joiner, so Japanese and Chinese have no space after their full
stop. Dates use a format each language supplies: the full month name in the
form the language writes after a day, or numbers where the month name would
need an elided article (Italian, Catalan) or end in a dot that doubles the
full stop (Lithuanian). Prices use a translatable "$%(amount)s".

The catalogs are machine-translated and marked "# AI Translated". The
compiled .mo files are committed (a .gitignore exception), as Obico's are,
because the web image doesn't compile catalogs; test_language.py fails when
an entry is untranslated or a .mo is behind its .po. The README's "JusPrin
2's server text" section says how to update them.

Chargebee's checkout and receipts, Obico's own sign-in pages, and the plan
names Hobby and Workshop stay English.

=== bcd0fc94b0 JusPrin 2: report every failure a person cannot act on, and take the app's error reports
A failure the person can do nothing about is answered "Something went wrong
on our side" and goes to Sentry with everything known about it. A failure
they can act on keeps its own answer. Kenneth, 2026-11-16: "if the error is
something that user can do nothing about, just show the user a generic error
message and give user a way to report a problem. On the back end though, we
need to make sure we send as much info as possible to the Sentry server so
that we can do root cause analysis. And that's it, nothing else."

The AI gateway (/ent/jusprin/v2/messages and /responses):
- The provider refusing a request (any status but 200 and 413), failing or
  going quiet partway through a reply, being unreachable or too slow, and the
  server's own slots for large requests being full all reach the one handler
  at the top of the endpoint. Before, a 400 was passed off as a 502, a
  failure inside a reply was recorded as a completed reply, and an outage or
  a timeout got an answer of its own and reached no Sentry.
- A completed reply that cannot be kept afterwards, and a chat title the app
  did not encode as UTF-8, reach the same handler. Before, the first was
  caught where it happened and the second was read with its bad bytes
  replaced.
- The report carries the provider's status, request id and error text, and
  the request's user, chat, turn, kind, alias, model and outcome.
- None of these is recorded as a completed reply or kept as one.
- Answers of their own, in errors.EXPECTED: signed out, out of credits, app
  too old, too many turns a minute, chat too large for the provider, and the
  four refusals of a print report.

The Django views: a failure reaches Sentry through its Django integration.
The app is told the same sentence as JSON; a page in the app's sheet shows it
in the app's language.

Checkout and cancel: Chargebee refusing a checkout or a cancel is not the

input.content:
JusPrin 2.0.1 speaks your language, connects more printers from the printer chat, and fixes printers that could not be added in languages that write decimals with a comma.

## New

- **JusPrin in your language.** JusPrin's own screens, the AI chat and Home are translated into the 22 languages OrcaSlicer ships. JusPrin uses the language you chose in Preferences. Numbers follow it too, for example "0,4 mm" in German. The translations are machine-made, so some wording may read oddly. AI still answers in the language you write to it.
- **More printers connect from the printer chat.** The printer chat can now connect every connection type OrcaSlicer's printer settings offer, not only Klipper (Moonraker) and OctoPrint. This includes Elegoo Centauri Carbon and Centauri Carbon 2 printers (Elegoo Link). The chat cannot finish Repetier, UltiMaker, or PrusaLink with a user name and password, and tells you where to set those up instead. Obico, SimplyPrint and 3DPrinterOS still need their own sign-in.
- **Reporting errors.** When something goes wrong that you can't fix yourself, JusPrin shows one message, "Something went wrong on our side". You can see the whole report, then press Report to JusPrin team, or tick "From now on, report errors like this automatically". You can also turn this on or off in Preferences › Updates › Error reports. It is off until you turn it on.

## Fixed

- In languages that write decimals with a comma, such as German, French, Spanish, Portuguese and Russian, the add-printer form showed no nozzle sizes for most printers, so the printer could not be added. Bed sizes such as 233.5 mm were also read as 233 mm, and a 0.4 mm nozzle in an opened 3MF file was read as 0. This always happened on Windows.
- A calibration test started from one of your projects lost that project and its chat.
- A project could save itself again after sitting idle, with nothing changed.
- A file the AI chat refused to attach (too large, or a kind it can't read) stopped the project from saving until you removed it.
- If JusPrin couldn't write its settings file, signing in or saving an API key looked like it worked, and was lost when you quit. Preferences now says it couldn't be kept.
- Deleting your account now waits while AI is still replying in the main window.
- A chat whose account or API key was removed showed the wrong model in its greyed-out model picker. It now shows the model the chat ran on.
- When AI prepared a print, it could keep checking the slice it had just started, again and again, while the slice ran.

## What JusPrin now sends

- **When the app starts**, it tells JusPrin's server once that it started: a random number made on the first start, the app's version and the name of your operating system. Nothing in it names you, and no sign-in goes with it. It is not sent in stealth mode.
- **Error reports and crashes** go to JusPrin's error tracker (Sentry) only when you press Report to JusPrin team, or when you have turned on automatic reports. A report holds where in the app the error happened, your computer's system and the app's log for that run. A crash report also holds the state of the app when it crashed. With automatic reports off, a crash report stays on your computer.

## Downloads

- **Windows (64-bit):** the installer, or the portable .zip, which runs without installing.
- **Mac:** one disk image for Macs with Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
- **Linux (64-bit):** an AppImage, built on Ubuntu 24.04. Make the file executable, then run it.
- **SHA256SUMS.txt** lists each file's checksum.

Questions or problems: write to jusprin-support@obico.io, or use Help › Report a problem in the app.

2	
3	## New
4	
5	- **JusPrin in your language.** JusPrin's own screens, the AI chat and Home are translated into the 22 languages OrcaSlicer ships. Choose the language in Preferences › Appearance › Language. Numbers follow it too, for example "0,4 mm" in German. The translations are made by machine, so some wording may read oddly.
6	- **More printers connect from the printer chat.** The printer chat can now connect every connection type OrcaSlicer's printer settings offer, not only Klipper (Moonraker) and OctoPrint. This includes Elegoo Centauri Carbon and Centauri Carbon 2 printers (Elegoo Link). The chat cannot finish Repetier, UltiMaker, or PrusaLink with a user name and password, and tells you where to set those up instead. Obico, SimplyPrint and 3DPrinterOS still need their own sign-in.
7	- **Reporting errors.** When something goes wrong that you can't fix yourself, JusPrin shows one message, "Something went wrong on our side". You can see the whole report, then press Report to JusPrin team, or tick "From now on, report errors like this automatically". You can also turn this on or off in Preferences › Updates › Error reports. It is off until you turn it on.
8	
9	## Fixed
10	
11	- In languages that write decimals with a comma, such as German, French, Spanish, Portuguese and Russian, the add-printer form showed no nozzle sizes for most printers, so the printer could not be added. Bed sizes such as 233.5 mm were also read as 233 mm, and a 0.4 mm nozzle in an opened 3MF file was read as 0. This always happened on Windows.
12	- A calibration test started from one of your projects lost that project and its chat.
13	- A project could save itself again after sitting idle, with nothing changed.
14	- A file the AI chat refused to attach (too large, or a kind it can't read) stopped the project from saving until you removed it.
15	- If JusPrin couldn't write its settings file, signing in or saving an API key looked like it worked, and was lost when you quit. JusPrin now shows an error instead.
16	- Deleting your account now waits until AI has finished replying in any chat.
17	- A chat whose account or API key was removed showed the wrong model in its greyed-out model picker. It now shows the model the chat ran on.
18	- When AI prepared a print, it could keep checking the slice it had just started, again and again, while the slice ran.
19	
20	## What JusPrin now sends
21	
22	- **When the app starts**, it tells JusPrin's server once that it started: a random number made on the first start, the app's version and the name of your operating system. Nothing in it names you, and no sign-in goes with it. It is not sent in stealth mode.
23	- **Error reports and crashes** go to JusPrin's error tracker (Sentry) only when you press Report to JusPrin team, or when you have turned on automatic reports. A report holds where in the app the error happened, the steps just before it (never what you typed or what AI said), your operating system and the app's log for that run. A crash report also holds the app's state at the moment it crashed. With automatic reports off, a crash report stays on your computer.
24

27	- **Windows (64-bit):** the installer, or the portable .zip, which runs without installing.
28	- **Mac:** one disk image for Macs with Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
29	- **Linux (64-bit):** an AppImage, built on Ubuntu 24.04. Make the file executable, then run it.

# JusPrin error handling: audit

The rules are the Error handling section of `AGENTS.md` (JusPrin, the desktop
app) and of `CLAUDE.md` (tsd-enterprise, the JusPrin Cloud server). Read that
section first; this skill only says how to check code against it. Checking
production for failures over a period is the `jusprin-production-check` skill
in the tsd-enterprise repository.

The server's expected-errors table is `EXPECTED` in
`web_ent/jusprin/v2/errors.py`; the app has no table yet. The app reports
through `report_unexpected_error`, the server through Sentry. List an outcome
that looks designed but has no table entry apart from the other findings.

## Audit a commit range

Input: a repository and a range, such as `jusprin/v2.0.0..jusprin-dev`.

The audit is one question, asked of every place the changed code decides what
happened: **can the person do something about it, and did Kenneth decide what
they are told?** Do not search for particular
code shapes. Each failure this audit exists for had a shape nobody had listed,
and a list only finds what its writer already thought of.

1. List the changed code: `git diff --stat <range>`, then read each changed
   function whole in JusPrin's own code (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, the
   pages, `web_ent/jusprin/`). Read the function, not the diff lines: what a
   change leaves the rest of the function to assume is where failures hide.
2. Wherever the code decides what happened (an outcome, a state, a record,
   what the person is told, whether work goes on), ask the question.
   - Yes to both: there is an entry in the expected-errors table for that
     named cause. Go to step 4.
   - Otherwise the code is dealing with an unexpected error. Go to step 3.
     A sentence, a code or a branch of its own for a failure the person can
     do nothing about (a provider or our server slow, overloaded, down or
     limiting us) is a finding, even when it looks carefully designed.
3. For an unexpected error the rules allow almost no code, so the code is
   the finding. Two things only are allowed:
   - turning a failure that arrived as a value into a thrown error on the
     spot, keeping the other side's status, request id and error text and
     the request's own facts (user, chat, turn, model), with no
     interpretation;
   - the one handler at the top of an entry point, which reports through the
     reporting function and tells the person "Something went wrong on our
     side", with nothing more specific.
   Everything else is a finding: work that goes on after a failure nobody
   decided on, a value or a sentence invented for it, a retry, a report call
   anywhere but the top handler, a failure recorded as a success, and the
   other side's status, request id or error text dropped on the way up. Also
   follow one failure up from each entry point the change touches and say
   whether it reaches a handler that reports it and tells the person.
4. Read every new or changed entry in the expected-errors tables, and every
   place that catches. Flag an entry whose cause is a status code, an
   exception type or "the request was not valid", an entry the person can do
   nothing about, two entries that leave the person doing the same thing, an
   entry with no test, and
   an entry added without Kenneth's quoted yes in its commit message. Flag a
   catch that is neither recovering from an expected error nor translating
   at a boundary and rethrowing.
5. Report each finding as `file:line`, the rule it breaks, and what a person
   or the record would see go wrong. Say which findings you checked by
   running code and which only by reading. Code older than the range is not
   a finding of this audit; name it separately if it matters.

You are auditing one part of a JusPrin release (desktop 3D-printing slicer app, C++, a fork of OrcaSlicer) against its error-handling rules. READ-ONLY: do not edit, commit, build or run anything that changes files. Work in /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/release-2.0.1 (a git worktree; do not cd to the main checkout).

First read the "Error handling" section of AGENTS.md in that folder, then follow .claude/skills/error-handling/SKILL.md exactly (it says how to audit; its one question is: wherever changed code decides what happened, can the person do something about it, and did Kenneth decide what they are told?).

Range: jusprin/v2.0.0..HEAD. Your scope is only these folders under src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/: Support/, Shell/, Updates/, Home/, PrintIssues/, PrinterSetup/, Printers/, Canvas/, Web/, WebShared/, Brand/, plus the two OrcaSlicer files src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/WebView.{hpp,cpp}. Skip tests, .po/.pot catalogs and .md files. Pay special attention to Support/ErrorReport, Support/SentryClient, Support/ThrowStack, Support/PageScheme (the top handlers and the reporting path itself), Updates/LaunchReport, and the printer-connection code (printer_host_connect for every host type). List changed files with `git diff --stat jusprin/v2.0.0..HEAD -- <folder>`, then read each changed function whole (not only the diff lines). Commit messages (`git log jusprin/v2.0.0..HEAD -- <folder>`) quote Kenneth's decisions; a designed outcome is allowed only where Kenneth's quoted yes covers it. Code older than the range is not a finding; mention it separately only if it matters.

Report back (under ~600 words): each finding as file:line, the rule it breaks, and what a person or the error record would see go wrong; mark each as checked by reading only. Most serious first. If you find nothing in an area, say so.

# Windows GUI test VM (GCP) — working harness

Drives a wxWidgets + OpenGL desktop app on a GPU-less Windows VM in GCP,
headlessly: launch it, screenshot it, click it, verify the result.

Verified 2026-09-07 with OrcaSlicer 2.4.2 portable.

## The VM

    instance : jusprin-win-test
    project  : elegoo-backend
    zone     : us-central1-a
    machine  : n2-standard-8, Windows Server 2022, 100GB pd-balanced
    display  : virtual display device ENABLED (required, see below)
    login    : ssh as guitest with ~/.ssh/google_compute_engine

The external IP is ephemeral and CHANGES on every stop/start. Re-read it with:

    gcloud compute instances describe jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a \
      --project=elegoo-backend \
      --format="value(networkInterfaces[0].accessConfigs[0].natIP)"

then update winssh.sh / winscp.sh.

## Four things that had to be solved

1. **OpenGL.** The app hard-requires OpenGL 3.2 (src/slic3r/GUI/OpenGLManager.cpp)
   and exits below it. Stock Windows software rendering reports 1.1. Fix: drop
   Mesa's `opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` (from pal1000/mesa-dist-win) next
   to the .exe. Reports OpenGL 4.2 on plain CPU.

   Mesa then auto-picks its **d3d12** backend, because the GCE virtual display
   exposes "Microsoft Basic Render Driver" as a D3D12 device — and that path
   crashed on the first frame. run-app.cmd forces the CPU rasterizer with
   `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`.

   Do NOT copy the whole Mesa .7z onto the VM: Windows Defender flags the archive
   as Trojan:Win32/Suschil!rfn and deletes it. Extract the two DLLs elsewhere and
   copy just those — Defender does not object to them, so no AV exclusion is
   needed. (The archive's sha256 matches GitHub's published release digest; the
   detection is a heuristic on the bundle, which also contains Vulkan layers,
   D3D12 compilers and media-foundation encoders we don't use.)

2. **A visible desktop.** A GUI app started from an SSH shell lands in a session
   with no desktop and screenshots come back black. autologon.ps1 creates a local
   admin `guitest` and sets Winlogon AutoAdminLogon so console session 1 is always
   live. Something in the GCE image clears those values after the boot that sets
   them, so startup.ps1 re-applies them on EVERY boot.

3. **Session isolation.** Display APIs, EnumWindows and Get-Process MainWindowTitle
   only see the CALLING session's window station. Run them over SSH and they
   silently report nothing — which reads as "the app has no window" when it does.
   Everything that touches the UI goes through `Invoke-InSession` in harness.ps1,
   which registers a scheduled task with `-LogonType Interactive` so it runs in
   session 1, and writes its output to a file to be read back over SSH.

4. **Resolution.** Without a GCE virtual display device the guest falls back to
   Microsoft Basic Display Adapter with no EDID = 640x480, and the app's own
   window is 760x500. Fix (requires the instance to be STOPPED):

       gcloud compute instances stop   jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a --project=elegoo-backend
       gcloud compute instances update jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a --project=elegoo-backend --enable-display-device
       gcloud compute instances start  jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a --project=elegoo-backend

   Then 1920x1080 is available via set-res.ps1.

## Also required by this app

Microsoft Edge WebView2 runtime is NOT present on a clean Windows Server image.
Without it the app puts up a modal "WebView2 Runtime" prompt and startup blocks
forever. Installed here as 152.0.4191.66 via the Evergreen bootstrapper:

    Invoke-WebRequest "https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/p/?LinkId=2124703" -OutFile setup.exe
    .\setup.exe /silent /install

This matters more for JusPrin than for stock Orca, since JusPrin's UI is
WebView-based.

## Files

    startup.ps1      GCE windows-startup-script-ps1: OpenSSH, port 22 firewall,
                     authorized_keys, calls autologon.ps1. Runs every boot.
    autologon.ps1    Creates guitest + sets AutoAdminLogon. Idempotent.
    harness.ps1      Invoke-InSession / Take-Screenshot. Source this first.
    screenshot.ps1   Screen capture. Must run in-session.
    probe.ps1        Lists session 1's real windows to C:\guitest\windows.txt.
    focus-app.ps1    Closes leftover task consoles, maximizes the app window.
    click.ps1        Clicks the "x,y" in C:\guitest\click.txt.
    set-res.ps1      Sets 1920x1080. Must run in-session.
    install-app.ps1  Downloads the app, places the Mesa DLLs beside the .exe.
    run-app.cmd      Launches the app with llvmpipe forced, detached.
    winssh.sh        ssh wrapper. winscp.sh: scp wrapper.

## Typical cycle

    ./winscp.sh <local.ps1> guitest@<IP>:C:/guitest/
    ./winssh.sh '. C:\guitest\harness.ps1; Invoke-InSession -TaskName "X" ...'
    ./winssh.sh '. C:\guitest\harness.ps1; Take-Screenshot'
    ./winscp.sh guitest@<IP>:C:/guitest/shot.png ./shot.png

## Known gap

There is no current JusPrin Windows binary to test. The Build all workflow's
Windows job fails at `cmake -G "Visual Studio 17 2022"` with "could not find any
instance of Visual Studio"; last green Windows build was 2026-03-04 and its
artifacts have expired. Either fix that job, or install VS Build Tools on this VM
and build from the cached OrcaSlicer_dep_win64 artifact.

# Building JusPrin from source on the Windows VM

Verified 2026-09-07: full build from a clean VM, then run and screenshotted.
Total ~1h10m of machine time on n2-standard-16 (16 vCPU, 64 GB).

    deps build   22.7 min   (all 24 applicable deps from source)
    slicer build 23.0 min
    output       C:\src\JusPrin\build\src\Release\orca-slicer.exe (261 KB launcher)
                 + OrcaSlicer.dll (122.7 MB — the actual application)

## Order of operations

1. `install-buildtools.ps1` — CMake 4.3.5 (CI pins ~4.3.0), Ninja, Git for
   Windows, Strawberry Perl, and VS 2022 Build Tools with the VCTools workload.
2. Clone the repo (public, no credentials needed). Shallow is fine: the version
   comes from `version.inc`, not git tags.
3. `build-deps-full.ps1` — builds all deps. **Do not use the CI dependency
   artifact**; see below.
4. `build-slicer.ps1` — runs `build_release_vs.bat slicer`.
5. Put Mesa where the app looks for it, then `run-jusprin.cmd`.

## Things that will bite you

**Run long builds as a SCHEDULED TASK, not over SSH.** Windows OpenSSH kills the
whole process tree when the session ends, so a build started from an SSH command
(even detached with Start-Process) dies on disconnect. Register it instead:

    New-ScheduledTaskPrincipal -UserId "SYSTEM" -LogonType ServiceAccount -RunLevel Highest

Two builds racing in one directory corrupt each other — OpenSSL failed with
`C1033: cannot open program database ossl_static.pdb` when that happened here.

**awk must be on PATH.** `deps/PNG/PNG.cmake` passes `-DPNG_PREFIX=prusaslicer_`,
so libpng generates `pngprefix.h` with an awk script. Without awk you get
`AWK-NOTFOUND` in the PNG CMakeCache and then `C1083: Cannot open include file:
'pngprefix.h'`. Git for Windows ships awk — add `C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin`
to PATH, not just `C:\Program Files\Git\cmd`.

**Set `CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5`.** Several bundled CMakeLists still
declare pre-3.5 minimums, which CMake 4.x rejects outright.

**The CI dependency artifact is unusable.** `OrcaSlicer_dep_win64_20260906`
contains a bundle built 2025-10-17, before `deps/Eigen` was added. The source
requires Eigen 5.0.1 and CMake fails at configure with "Could not find a package
configuration file provided by Eigen3". Build deps from source instead.

**Never hard-stop the VM mid-build.** Stopping the instance during the deps build
left 622 of 22,011 installed files as NUL bytes. It surfaced as bogus syntax
errors deep in Boost headers. Detect it with:

    Get-ChildItem $prefix -Recurse -Include *.hpp,*.h,*.cmake |
      # read first 4 KB, flag any file containing byte 0

The fix is a clean rebuild; DL_CACHE keeps all 21 source archives, so it is a
recompile, not a re-download.

**Qhull is expected to be missing.** `deps/CMakeLists.txt` comments it out under
`if (MSVC)` ("Experimental"), so 24 built deps is the complete set on Windows.

## Running it — use the app's own Mesa hook

Do NOT drop opengl32.dll next to the exe. `src/OrcaSlicer_app_msvc.cpp` already
handles this: when system OpenGL is below 2.0 it loads `<exedir>\mesa\opengl32.dll`
itself and prints "MESA OpenGL library was loaded successfully".

    build\src\Release\mesa\opengl32.dll      <- Mesa's, the app loads this
    build\src\Release\libgallium_wgl.dll     <- dependency, resolves from exe dir

Still export `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`: the GCE
virtual display exposes a D3D12 device, and Mesa's d3d12 backend crashes on the
first rendered frame.

## Windows CI is broken for a different reason

`Build all`'s Windows job fails at `cmake -G "Visual Studio 17 2022"` with
"could not find any instance of Visual Studio". That is NOT a bug in
`build_release_vs.bat` — the same script picks generator VS 17 2022 here from
`msbuild -version` (17.14.51.32402) and configures fine against a registered
Build Tools instance. The problem is the GitHub runner's environment.
#!/bin/bash
ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o IdentitiesOnly=yes \
    -o ConnectTimeout=15 -o LogLevel=ERROR -i ~/.ssh/google_compute_engine \
    guitest@34.135.245.169 "$@"

---
name: windows-build-on-gcp-vm
description: JusPrin builds and runs on the GCP Windows VM; the five traps that make it fail, and why the CI Windows job failing is a runner-environment problem, not a script bug.
metadata:
  type: project
---

JusPrin compiles from source on the Windows test VM and the built binary runs
with its Agent UI visible. Verified 2026-09-07 on n2-standard-16: deps 22.7 min,
slicer 23.0 min. Output is `orca-slicer.exe` (261 KB launcher) plus
`OrcaSlicer.dll` (122.7 MB). Full recipe in
`/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/vm-harness/windows/BUILDING.md`; VM setup in its README.
See [[windows-gui-test-vm-gcp]].

**Why:** four of the five failures below produce misleading errors far from
their cause, and two were self-inflicted by how the build was driven.

**How to apply:**
- Run long builds as a Windows **scheduled task** (SYSTEM / ServiceAccount), not
  over SSH — OpenSSH kills the process tree on disconnect. Never let two builds
  share a directory: that produced OpenSSL `C1033 cannot open program database`.
- Add `C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin` to PATH so **awk** is found, or libpng
  cannot generate `pngprefix.h` (`-DPNG_PREFIX=` in deps/PNG/PNG.cmake) and you
  get a confusing `C1083` on a header that was never written.
- Set `CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5` for CMake 4.x.
- **Do not use the CI deps artifact** — the shipped bundle predates `deps/Eigen`
  and cannot satisfy Eigen 5.0.1. Build deps from source.
- Never hard-stop the VM mid-build: doing so left 622 installed files full of
  NUL bytes and surfaced as fake syntax errors inside Boost headers.
- Qhull is deliberately excluded on MSVC (deps/CMakeLists.txt), so 24/25 is
  complete on Windows.
- To run headless, use the app's own hook rather than dropping DLLs beside the
  exe: `src/OrcaSlicer_app_msvc.cpp` loads `<exedir>\mesa\opengl32.dll` when
  system OpenGL < 2.0. Still force `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe`.

The `Build all` Windows CI job fails at `cmake -G "Visual Studio 17 2022"` with
"could not find any instance of Visual Studio". That is a GitHub runner

# JusPrin Linux GUI test VM

A GCP VM for building JusPrin on Linux and testing its GUI, either by hand over
remote desktop or by script on a headless display.

| | |
|---|---|
| Instance | `jusprin-linux-test`, project `elegoo-backend`, zone `us-west2-a` (Los Angeles, for low latency from California) |
| Machine | n2-standard-16 (16 vCPU, 64 GB), 300 GB pd-balanced, no GPU |
| OS | Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, XFCE desktop |
| Toolchain | Ubuntu's gcc 13, CMake 4.3.0 (same as the CI runner, in /opt), Node 24.11.1 (in /opt) |
| Checkout | `~/JusPrin` on branch `jusprin-dev` (user `kenneth`) |
| OpenGL | Mesa llvmpipe, OpenGL 4.5 core, software rendering |

The VM has no service account, so it cannot call GCP APIs. It cannot fetch the
private GitHub repo either; send commits with a git bundle (below).

## Scripts (run on the Mac)

- `./vmssh.sh '<command>'` runs a command on the VM.
- `./vmscp.sh <src> <dst>` copies files; write `VM:~/path` for the VM side.
- `./connect-rdp.sh` starts the VM if stopped, prints the login, and holds an SSH
  tunnel open. Point Windows App (Microsoft Remote Desktop) at `localhost:33890`,
  user `kenneth`. xrdp listens only on the VM's own localhost, so the project-wide
  `default-allow-rdp` firewall rule does not expose it.
- `env.sh` holds the instance name and forces the `ai-agent` service account. It
  also points gcloud at uv's standalone Python 3.12, because Homebrew's Python lost
  its OpenSSL library when Homebrew moved from openssl@3 to openssl@4.

## Scripts (copied to the VM's home folder)

- `~/vm-run-app.sh [args]` starts the built app on headless display `:99` (Xvfb
  with the xfwm4 window manager) with data dir `~/jusprin-test-data`. Log:
  `~/app.log`. It sets `SSL_CERT_FILE`; without it OrcaSlicer's Linux build stops
  at startup on a dialog asking which certificate file to use.
- `~/vm-screenshot.sh` saves display `:99` to `~/shot.png`.
- Click with `DISPLAY=:99 xdotool mousemove X Y click 1`. Screenshot pixels equal
  screen coordinates (1920x1080).
- Stop the app with `pkill -x orca-slicer`. Never `pkill -f orca-slicer` over
  ssh: it matches the ssh command's own text and kills the session.

## Build

```bash
# First time on a fresh VM: deps (about 25 min) then app and tests (about 30 min)
cd ~/JusPrin && ./build_linux.sh -dst -j 16
# After code changes: app and tests only
cd ~/JusPrin && ./build_linux.sh -st -j 16
```

The app lands in `~/JusPrin/build/package/bin/orca-slicer`. Run long builds
detached so an ssh disconnect does not kill them:

```bash
setsid nohup bash -c 'set -o pipefail; ./build_linux.sh -st -j 16 2>&1 | tee ~/build.log; echo BUILD_EXIT=$? >> ~/build.log' >/dev/null 2>&1 </dev/null &
```

Tests: `cd ~/JusPrin/build && DISPLAY=:99 ctest -C Release -j 8`.

## Sending new commits

```bash
git bundle create f.bundle jusprin-dev ^<commit the VM already has>
./vmscp.sh f.bundle VM:~/
./vmssh.sh 'cd ~/JusPrin && git pull ~/f.bundle jusprin-dev'
```

## Cost

The VM bills while running. Stop it when idle:

```bash
gcloud compute instances stop jusprin-linux-test --project elegoo-backend --zone us-west2-a
```

The external IP is ephemeral and changes on each start; the scripts look it up
by name, so nothing needs editing.

PROJECT=elegoo-backend
ZONE=us-west2-a

[ -x "$UVPY" ] && export CLOUDSDK_PYTHON="$UVPY"

<result>I audited the five commits by reading the code at origin/master. I ran nothing. I found six problems, listed most serious first. The gateway's new top handler, the checkout and cancel changes, the server-error page, the start-report endpoint and the removal of the error-report endpoint all follow the rules. Every entry in `EXPECTED` has a test.

**Findings**

1. **`web_ent/jusprin/v2/errors.py:68-75`, plus where these are sent: `gateway.py:161-166` and `194-196`, and `upstream.py` `prepare`.** Your words in the code comment are "Treat them as unexpected errors", about `invalid_request`, `unknown_model` and `method_not_allowed`. The same commit keeps all three as refusals with sentences of their own. That breaks your decision and the rule that a message our own app sends and our server refuses is unexpected. Say the app sends a bad `X-JusPrin-Turn` header or a model the server no longer has. The person sees "The request is not valid." or "This model is not available.", not "Something went wrong on our side". Sentry hears nothing; there is only a log line with the code.

2. **`gateway.py:296-301`.** "Chat too large" is detected only by the provider answering 413. Anthropic's error docs say 413 means the request is over a size limit in bytes (32 MB). A chat that is too long for the model comes back as a 400; that comes from third-party error lists, not Anthropic's own docs. So the usual too-long chat goes to the generic handler, and the person sees "Something went wrong on our side". The entry promises "New chat, or fewer pictures", which they could actually do. The cause is being read from a status code, which the rules say is not a cause.

3. **`errors.py:60-62`, `already_reported`.** The entry's own next step is "Nothing". The rule written in the same commit (CLAUDE.md:20) says an error the person can do nothing about is unexpected. It still has its own sentence and its own 409.

4. **`errors.py:45-47`, `rate_limited`.** The next step is "Wait and retry". CLAUDE.md:20 says an error whose only next step is "try again later" is unexpected. You confirmed the table on 2026-11-15, the day before that rule was written, so only you can say whether this entry stays.

5. **`app_opened.py:44-48`, no quoted yes in commit c9e2b0af85.** Two outcomes here were designed without your quoted yes:
   - The day's "already sent" mark goes into the cache before the event is captured. If the capture fails, that person's "app opened" is lost for the day while the mark says it went out. That records a failure as a success.
   - The docstring says an event the library cannot deliver "is logged by the library and lost". A log line reaches nobody. A wrong key or an outage would stop every "app opened" event without anyone hearing about it.

6. **`stream.py:12`, minor, no table entry.** `response.incomplete` counts as a finished reply. A reply the provider cut short (output limit or content filter) is recorded as completed and kept, and nothing names that case. It may be the right call, but nobody decided it.

**Smaller point.** The table entries were added in commit bcd0fc94b0. That commit message quotes your 2026-11-16 words, but your 2026-11-15 "This table looks good. Confirmed." appears only in the code comment. The rules want it in the commit message.

**Older code (not part of this audit, but it matters)**
- `ledger/billing.py:155-157` (`card_line`, commit f880ea5076): if Chargebee fails, the billing page acts as if there is no card on file.
- `web.py:319` (`checkout_done`, commit f880ea5076): if the browser comes back from Chargebee signed out, the person lands on the prices page with no message. Purchases still depend on the webhook to be recorded.

Sources:
- [Claude API errors (Anthropic)](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors)
- [Portkey error library: input length error](https://portkey.ai/error-library/input-length-error-10153)</result>

$ErrorActionPreference = "Continue"
function Log($m) { $s = ("[SLICER {0:HH:mm:ss}] {1}" -f (Get-Date), $m); Write-Host $s; Add-Content C:\guitest\slicer-progress.txt $s }

$env:Path = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path","Machine")
$vswhere = "${env:ProgramFiles(x86)}\Microsoft Visual Studio\Installer\vswhere.exe"
$vsPath = & $vswhere -products * -requires Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.Tools.x86.x64 -property installationPath -latest
$env:Path = "$(Join-Path $vsPath 'MSBuild\Current\Bin');$env:Path"
# Several bundled CMakeLists still declare pre-3.5 minimums, which CMake 4.x
# rejects outright unless this compatibility shim is set.
$env:CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM = "3.5"

Set-Content C:\guitest\slicer-progress.txt "slicer build starting $(Get-Date -Format o)"
Log "msbuild: $((& msbuild -version) | Select-Object -Last 1)"
Set-Location C:\src\JusPrin
$sw = [Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
& cmd /c "build_release_vs.bat slicer 2>&1" | Tee-Object -FilePath C:\guitest\slicer-build.log
$code = $LASTEXITCODE
$sw.Stop()
Log ("build_release_vs.bat exit=$code elapsed={0:N1} min" -f $sw.Elapsed.TotalMinutes)

Log "--- executables produced ---"
