platform.description: The client platform the widget will render on. Pass 'mobile' when your system prompt indicates a mobile client (narrow ~380px viewport) so SVG viewBox and layout guidance are sized accordingly; otherwise pass 'desktop'. Defaults to 'unknown' (desktop sizing).

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: mcp__visualize__show_widget
tools.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

input.message:
Done: Mac runs are on hold, and the tainted arm64 deps are deleted. A fix for the Homebrew leak is committed and ready for Kenneth's decision.

- I had already started test run 44425355945 with a fix before your message arrived. I cancelled it. No build is running on Kenneth's Mac now.
- I deleted ~/Library/jusprin-ci/actions-runner/_work/_tool/jusprin-deps/arm64 (733 MB, the only folder kept there). No kept deps remain, so the next Mac run builds both architectures from scratch.
- Kenneth's keychain list is unchanged: /private/tmp/app-signing.keychain-db, then login.keychain-db.

The leak was worse than the Python modules. The arm64 app built on his Mac also loads OpenGL from XQuartz (/opt/X11/lib/libGL.1.dylib and libGLU), so it would not start on a Mac without XQuartz. FFmpeg's binaries in the deps link Homebrew's libX11 and SDL2.

I found two causes and tested both on his Mac:
- Homebrew's pkg-config hands its libraries to Python's and FFmpeg's builds.
- build_release_macos.sh joins its CMake ignore list with colons. CMake reads that as one folder that doesn't exist, so it still finds Homebrew's libb2 and OpenSSL. A semicolon list fixes it.

The fix is commit cee57ce080 on claude/self-hosted-mac-kept-deps, also copied to the pushed test branch claude/mac-runner-test. It changes only the self-hosted Mac steps:
- pkg-config looks only in the deps' own folder.
- The app build gets a semicolon ignore list that also names XQuartz's folders.
- A new script, src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/mac_outside_links.sh, stops the build if any program or library in the deps or the app loads something from outside macOS and the app itself. Kept deps that fail it are rebuilt.

I ran the script before relying on it. It flags every bad link in the tainted deps, in the arm64 app built on his Mac, and in his installed 2.0.0. Each scan takes under 10 seconds.

The shipped 2.0.0, built on GitHub's Macs, already has one leak: its Python _lzma loads /opt/homebrew/opt/xz. I proposed a separate session to fix the GitHub-hosted Mac path.

Rerunning the fix is one command, gh run rerun 44425355945. It's the test Kenneth needs to say yes to, and it takes about 2-3 hours. I won't start any Mac run until he decides. The nightly question is still open too: until the fix reaches jusprin-dev, each nightly's Mac jobs fail within seconds on his Mac, and the next one is at 07:35 UTC.

content.content:
# default keychain is left alone: on the self-hosted Mac those are its
      # owner's own, and a job stopped before its last step would otherwise
      # leave them changed.
      - name: Load the signing certificate
        if: env.SIGN == '1'
        env:
          BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64 }}
          P12_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.P12_PASSWORD }}
          KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          certificate="$RUNNER_TEMP/build_certificate.p12"
          keychain="$RUNNER_TEMP/app-signing.keychain-db"
          echo -n "$BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64" | base64 --decode --output "$certificate"
          security create-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$keychain"
          security set-keychain-settings -lut 21600 "$keychain"
          security unlock-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$keychain"
          security import "$certificate" -P "$P12_PASSWORD" -A -t cert -f pkcs12 -k "$keychain"
          read -r -a keychains <<< "$(security list-keychains -d user | xargs)"
          security list-keychains -d user -s "$keychain" "${keychains[@]}"
          security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple:,codesign: -s -k "$P12_PASSWORD" "$keychain"

      - name: Make the disk image
        env:
          JUSPRIN_SIGN: ${{ env.SIGN }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID }}
          APPLE_DEV_ACCOUNT: ${{ secrets.APPLE_DEV_ACCOUNT }}
          TEAM_ID: ${{ secrets.TEAM_ID }}
          APP_PWD: ${{ secrets.APP_PWD }}
        run: |
          ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/macos_package.sh \
            build/universal/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer.app "$VERSION" dist

      # Deletes the signing keychain, which also takes it off the search list,
      # even when an earlier step failed or the job was cancelled.
      - name: Remove the signing keychain
        if: always() && env.SIGN == '1'
        run: |
          keychain="$RUNNER_TEMP/app-signing.keychain-db"
          [ ! -e "$keychain" ] || security delete-keychain "$keychain"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: jusprin-macOS-universal
          path: dist/*.dmg
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

#!/bin/bash
# Sets up the macOS user that builds JusPrin's Mac release jobs, so that the
# builds never see the libraries in /opt/homebrew, /usr/local or XQuartz.
#
# Run it from Kenneth's own account, in Terminal:
#
#   sudo RUNNER_TOKEN="$(gh api -X POST repos/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/actions/runners/registration-token -q .token)" \
#     bash "<this file>"
#
# It asks for Kenneth's password (sudo), then for a password for the new
# account (sysadminctl). Nobody needs to log in as that account afterwards.
# Running it again skips what is already done.
#
# What it does:
# 1. Creates the standard (non-admin) user jusprin-ci, hidden from the login
#    window.
# 2. Clones Homebrew into /Users/jusprin-ci/homebrew and installs only the six
#    tools the deps build needs. Kenneth's /opt/homebrew is not touched.
# 3. Downloads the GitHub Actions runner into /Users/jusprin-ci/actions-runner,
#    checks its published SHA-256, and registers it with the label
#    jusprin-release-mac. Its PATH is that Homebrew plus macOS's own folders.
# 4. Runs it as a LaunchDaemon with UserName jusprin-ci, so it starts at boot
#    without anyone logging in as that user.
set -euo pipefail

ci_user=jusprin-ci
home=/Users/$ci_user
repo=TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin
label=jusprin-release-mac
name=kenneth-mac-jusprin-ci
runner_version=2.338.2
runner_sha=25a065af409ffa317ab4d5a3b614dd15fc9c40f2172bc1b35a1b1258e919a388
tools="automake libtool texinfo pkgconf yasm nasm"
path="$home/homebrew/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin"
plist=/Library/LaunchDaemons/com.jusprin.ci-runner.plist

if [ "$(id -u)" != 0 ]; then
  echo "Run this with sudo (see the top of the file)." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [ -z "${RUNNER_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
  echo "RUNNER_TOKEN is empty: run it as the top of the file shows." >&2
  exit 1
fi

as_ci() {
  sudo -u "$ci_user" env -i HOME="$home" USER="$ci_user" LOGNAME="$ci_user" LANG=en_US.UTF-8 \
    PATH="$path" HOMEBREW_NO_ANALYTICS=1 HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 HOMEBREW_NO_ENV_HINTS=1 "$@"
}

echo "== 1. The account"
if ! id "$ci_user" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "Type a password for the new account $ci_user:"
  sysadminctl -addUser "$ci_user" -fullName "JusPrin CI" -shell /bin/zsh -home "$home" -password -
  dscl . create "/Users/$ci_user" IsHidden 1
fi
createhomedir -c -u "$ci_user" > /dev/null
id "$ci_user"

echo "== 2. Its own Homebrew and the build tools"
if [ ! -x "$home/homebrew/bin/brew" ]; then
  as_ci git clone -q --depth 1 https://github.com/Homebrew/brew "$home/homebrew"
fi
# shellcheck disable=SC2086
as_ci "$home/homebrew/bin/brew" install $tools

echo "== 3. The runner"
runner=$home/actions-runner
as_ci mkdir -p "$runner" "$home/Library/Logs/jusprin-ci-runner"
if [ ! -x "$runner/config.sh" ]; then
  tarball=$runner/runner.tar.gz
  as_ci curl -fsSL -o "$tarball" \
    "https://github.com/actions/runner/releases/download/v$runner_version/actions-runner-osx-arm64-$runner_version.tar.gz"
  echo "$runner_sha  $tarball" | shasum -a 256 -c -
  as_ci tar -xzf "$tarball" -C "$runner"
  rm -f "$tarball"
fi
if [ ! -f "$runner/.runner" ]; then
  as_ci bash -c "cd '$runner' && ./config.sh --unattended --url 'https://github.com/$repo' \
    --token '$RUNNER_TOKEN' --name '$name' --labels '$label' --work _work"
fi
# Jobs get this PATH: never /opt/homebrew, /usr/local or /opt/X11.
echo "$path" | as_ci tee "$runner/.path" > /dev/null

echo "== 4. The service"
cat > "$plist" <<EOF
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
  <dict>
    <key>Label</key>
    <string>com.jusprin.ci-runner</string>
    <key>ProgramArguments</key>
    <array>
      <string>$runner/runsvc.sh</string>
    </array>
    <key>UserName</key>
    <string>$ci_user</string>
    <key>WorkingDirectory</key>
    <string>$runner</string>
    <key>RunAtLoad</key>
    <true/>
    <key>KeepAlive</key>
    <dict>
      <key>SuccessfulExit</key>
      <false/>
    </dict>
    <key>StandardOutPath</key>
    <string>$home/Library/Logs/jusprin-ci-runner/stdout.log</string>
    <key>StandardErrorPath</key>
    <string>$home/Library/Logs/jusprin-ci-runner/stderr.log</string>
    <key>EnvironmentVariables</key>
    <dict>
      <key>ACTIONS_RUNNER_SVC</key>
      <string>1</string>
      <key>HOME</key>
      <string>$home</string>
      <key>USER</key>
      <string>$ci_user</string>
      <key>LANG</key>
      <string>en_US.UTF-8</string>
      <key>PATH</key>
      <string>$path</string>
    </dict>
    <key>ProcessType</key>
    <string>Interactive</string>
    <key>SessionCreate</key>
    <true/>
  </dict>
</plist>
EOF
chown root:wheel "$plist"
chmod 644 "$plist"
launchctl bootout system "$plist" 2> /dev/null || true
launchctl bootstrap system "$plist"
sleep 5
launchctl print system/com.jusprin.ci-runner | grep -E "state|pid" | head -3
echo "Done. The runner $name should show as Idle on GitHub within a minute."

#!/bin/bash
# Sets up the macOS user that builds JusPrin's Mac release jobs, so that the
# builds never see the libraries in /opt/homebrew, /usr/local or XQuartz.
#
# Run it from Kenneth's own account, in Terminal:
#
#   sudo RUNNER_TOKEN="$(gh api -X POST repos/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/actions/runners/registration-token -q .token)" \
#     bash "<this file>"
#
# It asks for Kenneth's password (sudo), then for a password for the new
# account (sysadminctl). Nobody needs to log in as that account afterwards.
# Running it again skips what is already done.
#
# What it does:
# 1. Creates the standard (non-admin) user jusprin-ci, hidden from the login
#    window.
# 2. Clones Homebrew into /Users/jusprin-ci/homebrew and installs only the six
#    tools the deps build needs. Kenneth's /opt/homebrew is not touched.
# 3. Downloads the GitHub Actions runner into /Users/jusprin-ci/actions-runner,
#    checks its published SHA-256, and registers it with the label
#    jusprin-release-mac. Its PATH is that Homebrew plus macOS's own folders.
# 4. Runs it as a LaunchDaemon with UserName jusprin-ci, so it starts at boot
#    without anyone logging in as that user.
set -euo pipefail

ci_user=jusprin-ci
home=/Users/$ci_user
repo=TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin
label=jusprin-release-mac
name=kenneth-mac-jusprin-ci
runner_version=2.338.2
runner_sha=25a065af409ffa317ab4d5a3b614dd15fc9c40f2172bc1b35a1b1258e919a388
tools="automake libtool texinfo pkgconf yasm nasm"
path="$home/homebrew/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin"
plist=/Library/LaunchDaemons/com.jusprin.ci-runner.plist

if [ "$(id -u)" != 0 ]; then
  echo "Run this with sudo (see the top of the file)." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [ -z "${RUNNER_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
  echo "RUNNER_TOKEN is empty: run it as the top of the file shows." >&2
  exit 1
fi

as_ci() {
  sudo -u "$ci_user" env -i HOME="$home" USER="$ci_user" LOGNAME="$ci_user" LANG=en_US.UTF-8 \
    PATH="$path" HOMEBREW_NO_ANALYTICS=1 HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 HOMEBREW_NO_ENV_HINTS=1 "$@"
}

echo "== 1. The account"
if ! id "$ci_user" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "Type a password for the new account $ci_user:"
  sysadminctl -addUser "$ci_user" -fullName "JusPrin CI" -shell /bin/zsh -home "$home" -password -
  dscl . create "/Users/$ci_user" IsHidden 1
fi
createhomedir -c -u "$ci_user" > /dev/null
id "$ci_user"

echo "== 2. Its own Homebrew and the build tools"
if [ ! -x "$home/homebrew/bin/brew" ]; then
  as_ci git clone -q --depth 1 https://github.com/Homebrew/brew "$home/homebrew"
fi
# shellcheck disable=SC2086
as_ci "$home/homebrew/bin/brew" install $tools

echo "== 3. The runner"
runner=$home/actions-runner
as_ci mkdir -p "$runner" "$home/Library/Logs/jusprin-ci-runner"
if [ ! -x "$runner/config.sh" ]; then
  tarball=$runner/runner.tar.gz
  as_ci curl -fsSL -o "$tarball" \
    "https://github.com/actions/runner/releases/download/v$runner_version/actions-runner-osx-arm64-$runner_version.tar.gz"
  echo "$runner_sha  $tarball" | shasum -a 256 -c -
  as_ci tar -xzf "$tarball" -C "$runner"
  rm -f "$tarball"
fi
if [ ! -f "$runner/.runner" ]; then
  as_ci bash -c "cd '$runner' && ./config.sh --unattended --url 'https://github.com/$repo' \
    --token '$RUNNER_TOKEN' --name '$name' --labels '$label' --work _work"
fi
# Jobs get this PATH: never /opt/homebrew, /usr/local or /opt/X11.
echo "$path" | as_ci tee "$runner/.path" > /dev/null

echo "== 4. The service"
cat > "$plist" <<EOF
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
  <dict>
    <key>Label</key>
    <string>com.jusprin.ci-runner</string>
    <key>ProgramArguments</key>
    <array>
      <string>$runner/runsvc.sh</string>
    </array>
    <key>UserName</key>
    <string>$ci_user</string>
    <key>WorkingDirectory</key>
    <string>$runner</string>
    <key>RunAtLoad</key>
    <true/>
    <key>KeepAlive</key>
    <dict>
      <key>SuccessfulExit</key>
      <false/>
    </dict>
    <key>StandardOutPath</key>
    <string>$home/Library/Logs/jusprin-ci-runner/stdout.log</string>
    <key>StandardErrorPath</key>
    <string>$home/Library/Logs/jusprin-ci-runner/stderr.log</string>
    <key>EnvironmentVariables</key>
    <dict>
      <key>ACTIONS_RUNNER_SVC</key>
      <string>1</string>
      <key>HOME</key>
      <string>$home</string>
      <key>USER</key>
      <string>$ci_user</string>
      <key>LANG</key>
      <string>en_US.UTF-8</string>
      <key>PATH</key>
      <string>$path</string>
    </dict>
    <key>ProcessType</key>
    <string>Interactive</string>
    <key>SessionCreate</key>
    <true/>
  </dict>
</plist>
EOF
chown root:wheel "$plist"
chmod 644 "$plist"
launchctl bootout system "$plist" 2> /dev/null || true
launchctl bootstrap system "$plist"
sleep 5
launchctl print system/com.jusprin.ci-runner | grep -E "state|pid" | head -3
echo "Done. The runner $name should show as Idle on GitHub within a minute."

input.message:
The separate macOS user setup is ready. It now waits on Kenneth to run one command, because it needs his password. Please pass this on.

Already done on my side:
- The old runner is gone from Kenneth's account. I stopped and uninstalled its LaunchAgent, unregistered it from GitHub (the repo now has 0 runners), and deleted ~/Library/jusprin-ci and its logs.
- Commit cee57ce080, with mac_outside_links.sh, stays as the second guard.

What Kenneth runs, in Terminal from his own account (one command, two lines):

sudo RUNNER_TOKEN="$(gh api -X POST repos/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/actions/runners/registration-token -q .token)" \
  bash "/Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_55a7089d-34d6-4d0c-bc2e-c3745b488d0d/setup-jusprin-ci-user.sh"

It asks for his own password (sudo), then for a new password for the account it creates. Running it again skips anything already done. The script:
1. Creates jusprin-ci, a standard non-admin user hidden from the login window. It uses sysadminctl, and Kenneth types that user's password. Nobody needs to log in as it.
2. Clones a private Homebrew into /Users/jusprin-ci/homebrew. It installs only automake, libtool, texinfo, pkgconf, yasm and nasm, and doesn't touch /opt/homebrew. I tried this with a scratch Homebrew: automake, libtool, yasm and nasm install from Homebrew's ready-built packages outside /opt/homebrew. Texinfo and pkgconf build from source, a few minutes. I couldn't run those two builds from my session, because the Claude app's sandbox blocks Homebrew's own sandbox. Kenneth's Terminal has no such limit.
3. Downloads GitHub's runner 2.338.2 into /Users/jusprin-ci/actions-runner and checks its published SHA-256. It registers the runner as kenneth-mac-jusprin-ci with the same label, jusprin-release-mac, so the repo variable stays as it is. Jobs get the PATH "private Homebrew, then /usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin", never /opt/homebrew, /usr/local or /opt/X11.
4. Runs the runner as a LaunchDaemon, /Library/LaunchDaemons/com.jusprin.ci-runner.plist, with UserName jusprin-ci and SessionCreate. It starts at boot without anyone logging in.

Signing: the workflow already creates a throwaway keychain per job and deletes it at the end. Under jusprin-ci, that keychain only ever touches jusprin-ci's own search list, never Kenneth's. Signing and the disk image in a LaunchDaemon are untested until the Mac test run.

When Kenneth says it ran, I'll:
- check the runner shows Idle on GitHub
- run test run 44425355945 again (about 2-3 hours, both architectures rebuild their deps)
- watch it with a background gh run watch

Decision needed from Kenneth, still unanswered: should the nightly build keep using this Mac? Until the fix reaches jusprin-dev, each nightly's Mac jobs fail within seconds there. The next nightly is at 07:35 UTC. With no runner registered right now, its Mac jobs will wait in the queue and run once the new runner appears. My pick: leave the nightly on this Mac, since the failures stop once the fix lands. Should it stay?

- The runner is gone from your account. I stopped and removed its service, unregistered it from GitHub (the repo now has no runners), and deleted `~/Library/jusprin-ci` and its logs.
- The fix that keeps Homebrew and XQuartz libraries out of the build (commit cee57ce080) stays as a second guard.

**What you run.** In Terminal, from your own account, run this one command (it spans two lines):

```bash
sudo RUNNER_TOKEN="$(gh api -X POST repos/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/actions/runners/registration-token -q .token)" \
  bash "/Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_55a7089d-34d6-4d0c-bc2e-c3745b488d0d/setup-jusprin-ci-user.sh"
```

It asks for your password first, then for a password for the new account. You can run it again safely; it skips what's already done. It does four things:

1. **Creates the account.** `jusprin-ci` is a standard user, not an admin, and hidden from the login window. Nobody needs to log in as it.
2. **Gives it its own Homebrew.** It's in `/Users/jusprin-ci/homebrew`, with only the six build tools: automake, libtool, texinfo, pkgconf, yasm and nasm. Your `/opt/homebrew` isn't touched.
   - I tried this with a scratch Homebrew. automake, libtool, yasm and nasm install from Homebrew's ready-built packages there.
   - texinfo and pkgconf build from source, which takes a few minutes. I couldn't test those two from my session because the Claude app's sandbox blocks Homebrew's own sandbox. Your Terminal doesn't have that limit.
3. **Installs the GitHub runner** in `/Users/jusprin-ci/actions-runner`, after checking the download against GitHub's published checksum.
   - It keeps the same label, so the repo variable stays as it is.
   - Its jobs only search that private Homebrew and macOS's own folders. They never search `/opt/homebrew`, `/usr/local` or `/opt/X11`.
4. **Runs the runner as a system service** (a LaunchDaemon) under `jusprin-ci`, so it starts at boot without anyone logging in.

**Signing.** Each job already creates a throwaway signing keychain and deletes it at the end. Under `jusprin-ci`, that keychain never touches your own keychain list. Signing and building the disk image from a system service haven't been tested yet; the Mac test run will show whether they work.

name: JusPrin nightly

# Builds jusprin-dev, the development branch, once a day and puts the files
# on the "nightly-builds" pre-release, replacing the day before's, as
# JusPrin 1's "Build all" did.
#
# - GitHub runs scheduled workflows only on the default branch, main. The
#   scheduled run therefore only starts this workflow again on jusprin-dev,
#   so every step, OrcaSlicer's dependency build included, checks out
#   jusprin-dev.
# - The build is the release's (jusprin_build_all.yml), so a nightly is what a
#   release from the same commit would be. Its version is the one in
#   src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp.
# - Like a release, each platform's build fails without the Sentry secrets
#   and unless its debug files and the pages' source maps reach Sentry
#   (jusprin_release_build.yml).
# - The files keep JusPrin 1's nightly names, so download links stay the
#   same: JusPrin_Windows_Installer_nightly.exe,
#   JusPrin_Windows_nightly_portable.zip, JusPrin_Mac_universal_nightly.dmg,
#   JusPrin_Linux_AppImage_Ubuntu2404_nightly.AppImage, and SHA256SUMS.txt.
# - The nightly-builds tag moves to the commit built, and the release notes
#   name it. The scheduled build is skipped when jusprin-dev has not changed
#   since the last nightly.
# - The macOS app is signed and notarised; Windows builds are unsigned.
# - The app's update check never offers a nightly: it reads only tags named
#   vX.Y.Z and jusprin/vX.Y.Z (ReleaseFeed.cpp).
# - GitHub's hosted Apple-silicon macOS runners are often all taken in US
#   daytime, and GitHub cancels a job that gets none within 15 minutes. The
#   scheduled run lands in those hours, because this repo's schedules start
#   hours late. A run whose only failures are such jobs starts the nightly
#   again, up to 8 runs a day for one commit.
#
# Run it by hand from Actions > JusPrin nightly > Run workflow, with the
# branch set to jusprin-dev.

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '35 7 * * *' # near midnight US Pacific time, as JusPrin 1's nightly
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      sign_macos:
        description: 'Sign and notarise the macOS app with the Apple secrets'
        type: boolean
        default: true
      only_if_changed:
        description: 'Skip the build when jusprin-dev has not changed since the last nightly'
        type: boolean
        default: false

permissions:
  contents: write   # move the tag and replace the pre-release's files
  actions: write    # the scheduled run starts the build on jusprin-dev

concurrency:
  group: jusprin-nightly
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  TAG: nightly-builds

jobs:
  start:
    name: Start the build on jusprin-dev
    if: github.event_name == 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          gh workflow run jusprin_nightly.yml --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --ref jusprin-dev \
            -f sign_macos=true -f only_if_changed=true

  prepare:
    name: Check what to build
    # Only the development branch is published as the nightly.
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/jusprin-dev'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      build: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.build }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          sparse-checkout: src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'

      - name: Read the version
        id: version
        run: |
          echo "version=$(node src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release.mjs version src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp)" \
            | tee -a "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Skip an unchanged jusprin-dev
        id: changed
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          built=$(gh release view "$TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body | sed -n 's/^Commit: \([0-9a-f]*\).*/\1/p')
          if [ "${{ inputs.only_if_changed }}" = "true" ] && [ "$built" = "$GITHUB_SHA" ]; then
            echo "The nightly is already built from $GITHUB_SHA."
            echo "build=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "build=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  build:
    name: Build
    needs: prepare
    if: needs.prepare.outputs.build == 'true'
    uses: ./.github/workflows/jusprin_build_all.yml
    with:
      version: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}
      sign_macos: ${{ inputs.sign_macos }}
    secrets: inherit

  publish:
    name: Update the nightly-builds pre-release
    needs: [prepare, build]
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      VERSION: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}
      SIGNED_MACOS: ${{ inputs.sign_macos }}
    steps:
      - name: Collect the files
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: jusprin-*
          path: collected
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Give them the nightly names
        run: |
          mkdir dist
          for file in collected/*; do
            name=$(basename "$file")
            # The per-architecture Mac bundles only feed the universal app.
            case "$name" in JusPrin_Mac_bundle_*) continue ;; esac
            name=${name/_V$VERSION/_nightly}
            name=${name/_x64/}
            cp "$file" "dist/$name"
          done
          (cd dist && sha256sum -- * > SHA256SUMS.txt)
          cat dist/SHA256SUMS.txt

      - name: Replace the files and move the tag
        run: |
          gh release upload "$TAG" dist/* --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          gh api -X PATCH "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/tags/$TAG" -f sha="$GITHUB_SHA" -F force=true > /dev/null

      # Last, so the notes name a commit only once its files are up.
      - name: Write the notes
        run: |
          mac=$([ "$SIGNED_MACOS" = "true" ] && echo "signed and notarised" || echo "unsigned")
          cat > notes.md <<EOF
          The latest JusPrin $VERSION test build from jusprin-dev, the development branch, rebuilt every night. It may be broken; for a tested version, use the [latest release](https://github.com/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases/latest).

          - Windows: the installer or the portable zip. Unsigned, so Windows may warn before opening it.
          - macOS (Apple silicon and Intel): the disk image, $mac.
          - Linux (x64): the AppImage.

          Built $(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC') by [this run](https://github.com/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID).

          Commit: $GITHUB_SHA
          EOF
          gh release edit "$TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --title "JusPrin Nightly Builds" --notes-file notes.md

  retry:
    name: Start again when macOS got no runner
    needs: [prepare, build, publish]
    # Not after someone cancels the run. A job GitHub cancels for want of a
    # runner leaves the run failed, not cancelled.
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.prepare.outputs.build == 'true' && needs.publish.result != 'success' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      SIGN_MACOS: ${{ inputs.sign_macos }}
      MAX_RUNS: 8
    steps:
      - name: Start the nightly again
        run: |
          jobs=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID/attempts/$GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT/jobs?per_page=100" --jq '.jobs[]')
          # A job GitHub cancelled before any runner took it has no runner name.
          unstarted=$(jq -rs '[.[] | select(.conclusion == "cancelled" and (.runner_name // "") == "") | .name] | join(", ")' <<< "$jobs")
          failed=$(jq -rs '[.[] | select((.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled") and (.runner_name // "") != "") | .name] | join(", ")' <<< "$jobs")
          if [ -n "$failed" ]; then
            echo "Not starting again: these jobs failed on a runner: $failed"
            exit 0
          fi
          if [ -z "$unstarted" ]; then
            echo "Not starting again: no job went without a runner."
            exit 0
          fi
          since=$(date -u -d '24 hours ago' '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')
          runs=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/workflows/jusprin_nightly.yml/runs?branch=jusprin-dev&event=workflow_dispatch&head_sha=$GITHUB_SHA&created=>=$since" --jq .total_count)
          if [ "$runs" -ge "$MAX_RUNS" ]; then
            echo "::error::Not starting again: $runs nightly runs of $GITHUB_SHA in 24 hours. These jobs got no runner: $unstarted"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "These jobs got no runner: $unstarted. Starting run $((runs + 1)) of $MAX_RUNS."
          # It waits in the jusprin-nightly concurrency group until this run ends.
          gh workflow run jusprin_nightly.yml --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --ref jusprin-dev \
            -f sign_macos="$SIGN_MACOS" -f only_if_changed=true

#!/bin/bash
# Sets up the macOS user that builds JusPrin's Mac release jobs, so that the
# builds never see the libraries in /opt/homebrew, /usr/local or XQuartz.
#
# Run it from Kenneth's own account, in Terminal:
#
#   sudo RUNNER_TOKEN="$(gh api -X POST repos/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/actions/runners/registration-token -q .token)" \
#     bash "<this file>"
#
# It asks for Kenneth's password (sudo), then for a password for the new
# account (sysadminctl). Nobody needs to log in as that account afterwards.
# Running it again skips what is already done.
#
# What it does:
# 1. Creates the standard (non-admin) user jusprin-ci, hidden from the login
#    window.
# 2. Clones Homebrew into /Users/jusprin-ci/homebrew and installs only the six
#    tools the deps build needs. Kenneth's /opt/homebrew is not touched.
# 3. Downloads the GitHub Actions runner into /Users/jusprin-ci/actions-runner,
#    checks its published SHA-256, and registers it with the label
#    jusprin-release-mac. Its PATH is that Homebrew plus macOS's own folders.
# 4. Runs it as a LaunchDaemon with UserName jusprin-ci, so it starts at boot
#    without anyone logging in as that user.
set -euo pipefail

ci_user=jusprin-ci
home=/Users/$ci_user
repo=TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin
label=jusprin-release-mac
name=kenneth-mac-jusprin-ci
runner_version=2.338.2
runner_sha=25a065af409ffa317ab4d5a3b614dd15fc9c40f2172bc1b35a1b1258e919a388
tools="automake libtool texinfo pkgconf yasm nasm"
path="$home/homebrew/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin"
plist=/Library/LaunchDaemons/com.jusprin.ci-runner.plist

if [ "$(id -u)" != 0 ]; then
  echo "Run this with sudo (see the top of the file)." >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [ -z "${RUNNER_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
  echo "RUNNER_TOKEN is empty: run it as the top of the file shows." >&2
  exit 1
fi

as_ci() {
  sudo -u "$ci_user" env -i HOME="$home" USER="$ci_user" LOGNAME="$ci_user" LANG=en_US.UTF-8 \
    PATH="$path" HOMEBREW_NO_ANALYTICS=1 HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 HOMEBREW_NO_ENV_HINTS=1 "$@"
}

echo "== 1. The account"
if ! id "$ci_user" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "Type a password for the new account $ci_user:"
  sysadminctl -addUser "$ci_user" -fullName "JusPrin CI" -shell /bin/zsh -home "$home" -password -
  dscl . create "/Users/$ci_user" IsHidden 1
fi
createhomedir -c -u "$ci_user" > /dev/null
id "$ci_user"

echo "== 2. Its own Homebrew and the build tools"
if [ ! -x "$home/homebrew/bin/brew" ]; then
  as_ci git clone -q --depth 1 https://github.com/Homebrew/brew "$home/homebrew"
fi
# shellcheck disable=SC2086
as_ci "$home/homebrew/bin/brew" install $tools

echo "== 3. The runner"
runner=$home/actions-runner
as_ci mkdir -p "$runner" "$home/Library/Logs/jusprin-ci-runner"
if [ ! -x "$runner/config.sh" ]; then
  tarball=$runner/runner.tar.gz
  as_ci curl -fsSL -o "$tarball" \
    "https://github.com/actions/runner/releases/download/v$runner_version/actions-runner-osx-arm64-$runner_version.tar.gz"
  echo "$runner_sha  $tarball" | shasum -a 256 -c -
  as_ci tar -xzf "$tarball" -C "$runner"
  rm -f "$tarball"
fi
if [ ! -f "$runner/.runner" ]; then
  as_ci bash -c "cd '$runner' && ./config.sh --unattended --url 'https://github.com/$repo' \
    --token '$RUNNER_TOKEN' --name '$name' --labels '$label' --work _work"
fi
# Jobs get this PATH: never /opt/homebrew, /usr/local or /opt/X11.
echo "$path" | as_ci tee "$runner/.path" > /dev/null

echo "== 4. The service"
cat > "$plist" <<EOF
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
  <dict>
    <key>Label</key>
    <string>com.jusprin.ci-runner</string>
    <key>ProgramArguments</key>
    <array>
      <string>$runner/runsvc.sh</string>
    </array>
    <key>UserName</key>
    <string>$ci_user</string>
    <key>WorkingDirectory</key>
    <string>$runner</string>
    <key>RunAtLoad</key>
    <true/>
    <key>KeepAlive</key>
    <dict>
      <key>SuccessfulExit</key>
      <false/>
    </dict>
    <key>StandardOutPath</key>
    <string>$home/Library/Logs/jusprin-ci-runner/stdout.log</string>
    <key>StandardErrorPath</key>
    <string>$home/Library/Logs/jusprin-ci-runner/stderr.log</string>
    <key>EnvironmentVariables</key>
    <dict>
      <key>ACTIONS_RUNNER_SVC</key>
      <string>1</string>
      <key>HOME</key>
      <string>$home</string>
      <key>USER</key>
      <string>$ci_user</string>
      <key>LANG</key>
      <string>en_US.UTF-8</string>
      <key>PATH</key>
      <string>$path</string>
    </dict>
    <key>ProcessType</key>
    <string>Interactive</string>
    <key>SessionCreate</key>
    <true/>
  </dict>
</plist>
EOF
chown root:wheel "$plist"
chmod 644 "$plist"
launchctl bootout system "$plist" 2> /dev/null || true
launchctl bootstrap system "$plist"
sleep 5
launchctl print system/com.jusprin.ci-runner | grep -E "state|pid" | head -3
echo "Done. The runner $name should show as Idle on GitHub within a minute."

content.text:
The setup almost worked, but the runner can't start yet because of a mistake in my script, and the fix needs your password again.

These parts worked:
- The account `jusprin-ci` exists.
- Its own Homebrew has all six build tools.
- The runner is registered on GitHub with the right label.
- Jobs will only search that private Homebrew and macOS's own folders.

My mistake: the service starts `runsvc.sh` from the runner's folder, but my script never copied it there. The runner's own installer normally does that step, and my script skipped it. So the service exits at once with a configuration error, and GitHub shows the runner as offline.

I've fixed the script. Please run the same command again:

```bash
sudo RUNNER_TOKEN="$(gh api -X POST repos/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/actions/runners/registration-token -q .token)" bash "/Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_55a7089d-34d6-4d0c-bc2e-c3745b488d0d/setup-jusprin-ci-user.sh"
```

This time it only asks for your own password. It skips the account, the tool installs and the registration, copies `runsvc.sh` into place and restarts the service. If Homebrew asks "Do you want to proceed with the installation? [y/n]", answer `y`. That question is why the first run seemed stuck for half an hour.

I'm watching GitHub for the runner to come online, for up to 30 minutes. As soon as it does, I'll check it runs as `jusprin-ci`, then rerun the Mac test, which takes about 2–3 hours.

- **The Intel app compiled.**

**What I need from you.** I've added gettext to the setup script. Please run the same command again:

sudo RUNNER_TOKEN="$(gh api -X POST repos/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/actions/runners/registration-token -q .token)" bash "/Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_55a7089d-34d6-4d0c-bc2e-c3745b488d0d/setup-jusprin-ci-user.sh"
